lessons.title: What Is Philosophy?
lessons.blurb_en: The questions that are left when the facts run out, and the method Socrates invented for working on them.
lessons.blurb_zh: 事實用完之後還剩下的問題，以及蘇格拉底為了處理這些問題發明的方法。
lessons.big_en: Philosophy is the disciplined examination of the beliefs we rely on most and question least, carried out by giving reasons and testing them.
lessons.big_zh: 哲學是對我們最依賴、卻最少質疑的信念所做的嚴格檢驗；做法是提出理由，再檢驗理由。

paras.en: A four-year-old asks why the sky is dark at night, and you answer. She asks why the sun goes away, and you answer again. By the fifth why you have usually reached one of two walls. The first wall is ignorance: there is a fact of the matter, and you do not happen to know it. The second is stranger. You have run out of facts altogether, and what is left is a question such as why there is anything at all, or how you know you are not mistaken about all of it. No further observation would settle a question like that. Philosophy is what people do at the second wall.
paras.zh: 四歲的孩子問，為什麼晚上天是黑的，你回答了。她再問太陽為什麼會走掉，你又回答了。問到第五個「為什麼」，你通常會撞上兩種牆。第一種是無知：這件事有答案，只是你剛好不知道。第二種比較奇怪：事實整個用完了，剩下的是這樣的問題——為什麼會有東西存在，而不是什麼都沒有？你怎麼知道自己不是全盤都弄錯了？再多觀察也解決不了這種問題。人在第二道牆前面做的事，就是哲學。

paras.en: The word is Greek: philosophia, from philein, to love, and sophia, wisdom. An ancient story, told by Cicero some five centuries after the supposed event, credits it to Pythagoras, who is said to have declined the title sophos, wise man, and called himself only a lover of wisdom. The story is probably legend, but it has survived because it captures something true. A philosopher is defined by a relation to wisdom, and the relation is desire rather than possession.
paras.zh: 這個字是希臘文：philosophia，由 philein（愛）與 sophia（智慧）組成。有一個古老的故事說它出自畢達哥拉斯：他不肯接受 sophos（智者）的稱號，只說自己是「愛智慧的人」。這個故事是西塞羅在事隔約五百年後記下的，多半是傳說；它流傳下來，是因為說中了一件事。哲學家是由他跟智慧的關係來界定的，而那個關係是渴望，不是擁有。

paras.en: Plato has Socrates say that “philosophy begins in wonder” (Theaetetus 155d), and Aristotle agreed: “it is owing to their wonder that men both now begin and at first began to philosophize” (Metaphysics 982b). The wonder they had in mind is not the pleasant awe of a sunset. It is closer to puzzlement, the discomfort of noticing that something you took to be obvious does not, on inspection, make sense. Everyone knows what time is until asked to say. Everyone knows what a fair share is until two people claim the same thing.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖筆下的蘇格拉底說「哲學始於驚奇」（《泰阿泰德篇》155d），亞里斯多德也同意：「人們現在開始、以及最初開始做哲學思考，都是由於驚奇」（《形上學》982b）。他們說的驚奇，不是看夕陽時那種愉快的讚嘆，比較接近困惑：你發現一件向來以為理所當然的事，仔細一看竟然說不通，心裡因此不安。人人都知道時間是什麼，直到有人要他說出來。人人都知道什麼叫公平的一份，直到兩個人要同一樣東西。

paras.en: Socrates (c. 470–399 BCE) made a method of that discomfort. He wrote nothing. What we have are portraits by people who knew him, above all Plato, and in those portraits he does one thing again and again: he finds someone who claims to know what courage or justice or piety is, asks for a definition, and tests it against cases the speaker himself accepts. A general says that courage is standing firm in the line; Socrates points out that soldiers sometimes fight bravely while retreating. The definition is revised, tested again, and fails again.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底（約西元前 470–399 年）把這種不安變成一套方法。他一個字也沒寫。我們有的是認識他的人為他畫的像，其中最重要的是柏拉圖；在這些畫像裡，他反覆做同一件事：找到一個自稱知道什麼是勇敢、正義或虔敬的人，請對方下定義，再拿對方自己也承認的例子來檢驗這個定義。一位將軍說，勇敢就是在陣線上堅守不退；蘇格拉底指出，士兵有時是一邊撤退一邊英勇作戰的。定義修改了，再受檢驗，又垮了。

paras.en: The technical name for this cross-examination is the elenchus, and its usual result is aporia, a state of being at a loss. Socrates considered that result a gain. A person who has discovered that he does not know is at least in a position to start looking.
paras.zh: 這種詰問的術語叫 elenchus（詰問法），通常的結果是 aporia，也就是不知所措、無路可走的狀態。蘇格拉底認為這個結果是收穫。一個人發現自己並不知道，至少就站到了可以開始尋找的位置。

paras.en: Three neighbors help to mark the borders. Philosophy is not science, because its questions are not settled by measurement, though it reasons about what measurement can show. It is not religion, because it accepts no conclusion on authority, though it asks many of the same questions. And it is not mere opinion, because a philosophical claim has to be argued for, and an argument can be checked by anyone.
paras.zh: 有三個鄰居可以幫我們標出邊界。哲學不是科學，因為它的問題不是靠測量解決的，雖然它會推敲測量到底能證明什麼。哲學不是宗教，因為它不憑權威接受任何結論，雖然它問的許多問題跟宗教相同。哲學也不只是意見，因為哲學主張必須有論證支持，而論證是任何人都能檢查的。

paras.en: The discipline lives on that last point. You are free to believe whatever you like, but once you give reasons, your reasons become public property, and other people may show you that they do not support what you thought they did.
paras.zh: 這門學問就靠最後這一點活著。你愛相信什麼都可以；可是一旦你給出理由，你的理由就成了公共財，別人可以指給你看：這些理由並不支持你以為它們支持的結論。

paras.en: Over twenty-five centuries the questions have sorted themselves into branches. Logic studies what follows from what. Epistemology asks what knowledge is and whether we have any. Metaphysics asks what there is and what it is like: time, causation, the self, free will. Ethics asks how one should live, political philosophy how we should live together, and aesthetics what beauty and art are. Around these have grown the “philosophies of”: of mind, of language, of science, of religion, of education. The borders are porous. Ask whether a machine can think, and within a few minutes you will be doing metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics at once.
paras.zh: 兩千五百年下來，這些問題自己分成了幾個分支。邏輯學研究什麼可以從什麼推出來。知識論問知識是什麼、我們到底有沒有知識。形上學問有什麼東西存在、它們是什麼樣子：時間、因果、自我、自由意志。倫理學問人應該怎麼活，政治哲學問我們應該怎麼一起活，美學問美與藝術是什麼。在這些周圍又長出一批「某某哲學」：心靈哲學、語言哲學、科學哲學、宗教哲學、教育哲學。分支之間的邊界是透水的。問一句「機器會不會思考」，幾分鐘之內你就同時在做形上學、知識論和倫理學了。

paras.en: The Greek word should not mislead us about ownership. Confucius died about a decade before Socrates was born, and by then he had spent a lifetime asking what makes a person humane. The Buddha, whose dates are less certain, taught in the same era that what we call a self is a process and not a thing. Neither had a word for “philosophy.” The Chinese term 哲學 was coined only in 1874, by the Japanese scholar Nishi Amane, to translate the European word.
paras.zh: 這個字是希臘文，但我們不該因此弄錯這門學問歸誰所有。孔子過世大約十年後蘇格拉底才出生，而孔子已經用了一輩子追問：什麼使一個人成為仁者。佛陀的年代比較不確定，但他在同一個時代教導：我們稱為「我」的，是一個過程，不是一個東西。他們兩位都沒有「哲學」這個詞。中文的「哲學」要到 1874 年才出現，是日本學者西周為了翻譯這個歐洲字而造的。

paras.en: Yet a tradition does not need the label to do the work. Wherever people have given reasons for claims about knowledge, reality, and the good life, and have answered objections to them, philosophy has been going on. This series therefore follows three lines, Greek, Chinese, and Indian, and pays attention to the places where they meet.
paras.zh: 不過，一個傳統不需要有這個標籤，也能做這件工作。只要有人為自己關於知識、真實與美好人生的主張提出理由，並且回應別人的反駁，哲學就在進行。所以這個系列沿著三條線走：希臘、中國、印度，並且特別留意它們相遇的地方。

paras.en: Bertrand Russell faced the obvious complaint, that philosophy never seems to settle anything, and gave two replies. First, the complaint is partly an illusion: when a philosophical question becomes answerable, it gets a new name. Physics was once “natural philosophy”; psychology left home in the nineteenth century. What remains under the old name is, by definition, the unfinished business.
paras.zh: 最常見的抱怨是：哲學好像從來沒有解決過任何問題。羅素正面回應了這個抱怨，給了兩個答覆。第一，這個抱怨有一部分是錯覺：一個哲學問題一旦變得可以回答，就會換一個名字。物理學從前叫「自然哲學」；心理學是十九世紀才離家的。還留在舊名字底下的，按定義就是沒做完的事。

paras.en: Second, the unfinished business is worth doing for its own sake. Philosophy, he wrote, is to be studied “not for the sake of any definite answers to its questions,” but “for the sake of the questions themselves; because these questions enlarge our conception of what is possible.” A mind that has never doubted its own assumptions is confined by them. Socrates put the point more severely at his trial. The unexamined life, he told the jury, is not worth living.
paras.zh: 第二，沒做完的事本身就值得做。他寫道，研究哲學「不是為了它的問題有什麼確定的答案」，而是「為了這些問題本身；因為這些問題擴大了我們對於什麼是可能的想像」。一個從來沒有懷疑過自己預設的心靈，就被這些預設關住了。蘇格拉底在受審時把話說得更重。他對陪審團說：沒有經過省察的人生，不值得活。

lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：蘇格拉底式詰問
lab.lead_en: Three questions Socrates actually asked, with the answers his companions actually gave. Choose the definition you find most convincing and see what happens to it. Every step follows a dialogue of Plato; the reference is given under each reply.
lab.lead_zh: 這是蘇格拉底真的問過的三個問題，以及對話者真的給過的答案。選一個你覺得最有說服力的定義，看它會遇到什麼。每一步都依據柏拉圖的對話錄，出處標在每段回應下方。

dialogues.who_en: Socrates is talking with two Athenian generals, Laches and Nicias.
dialogues.who_zh: 蘇格拉底在跟兩位雅典將軍談話：拉凱斯與尼基亞斯。

defs.en: Courage is staying at your post and not running from the enemy.
defs.zh: 勇敢就是堅守崗位，不從敵人面前逃走。
defs.re_en: Then what about soldiers who fight while falling back? The Scythian horsemen fight as they retreat, and the Spartans at Plataea gave ground, then turned and won. And courage is not confined to battle: people are brave at sea, in illness, in poverty, and against their own desires. You have given me one kind of courage. I asked what all of them have in common.
defs.re_zh: 那麼一邊後退一邊作戰的士兵呢？斯基泰騎兵是邊退邊打的；斯巴達人在普拉提亞先讓出陣地，再回頭取勝。而且勇敢不限於戰場：人在海上、在病中、在貧困裡、在對抗自己的欲望時，都可以是勇敢的。你給我的是其中一種勇敢。我問的是它們全部的共同點。

defs.en: Courage is a kind of endurance of the soul.
defs.zh: 勇敢是靈魂的一種堅忍。
defs.re_en: You agree that courage is always something noble. But endurance can be foolish: a man who stubbornly holds on to a hopeless and harmful course is enduring, and we do not admire him. If foolish endurance counts, then courage is sometimes shameful, which you deny. So endurance alone cannot be what courage is.
defs.re_zh: 你同意勇敢永遠是高貴的。可是堅忍可以是愚蠢的：一個人固執地堅持一條沒有希望、而且有害的路，他是在堅忍，但我們並不欽佩他。如果愚蠢的堅忍也算，那勇敢有時就是可恥的，而這是你否認的。所以單是堅忍，不可能就是勇敢。

defs.en: Courage is knowledge of what is to be feared and what is to be hoped for.
defs.zh: 勇敢是一種知識：知道什麼該怕、什麼可以期待。
defs.flaw: Proves too much · 證明過頭
defs.re_en: What is to be feared is future evil, and what is to be hoped for is future good. But knowledge of good and evil is not divided by time; whoever has it knows past, present, and future goods and evils alike. A person with that knowledge would lack nothing of virtue: he would be just, temperate, and pious as well. So you have defined the whole of virtue, and we agreed at the start that courage is only a part of it.
defs.re_zh: 該怕的是未來的惡，可以期待的是未來的善。可是關於善惡的知識不分時間；有這種知識的人，對過去、現在、未來的善惡一樣明白。有這種知識的人，在德行上什麼都不缺：他同時也會是正義的、節制的、虔敬的。所以你定義的是德行的全部，而我們一開始就同意，勇敢只是德行的一部分。

dialogues.end_en: “Then, Nicias, we have not discovered what courage is.” The dialogue ends there. Two generals who have shown courage all their lives cannot say what it is.
dialogues.end_zh: 「那麼，尼基亞斯，我們還沒有發現勇敢是什麼。」對話到此結束。兩位一輩子都表現出勇敢的將軍，說不出勇敢是什麼。

dialogues.who_en: Socrates is at the house of the old merchant Cephalus, with his son Polemarchus and the sophist Thrasymachus.
dialogues.who_zh: 蘇格拉底在老商人克法洛斯家中，在場的還有他的兒子波勒馬科斯與智者特拉敘馬科斯。

defs.en: Justice is telling the truth and giving back what you owe.
defs.zh: 正義就是說實話，並且歸還你所欠的。
defs.re_en: Suppose a friend lends you his weapon while he is in his right mind, and asks for it back after he has gone mad. Everyone would say that you ought not to return it, and that you ought not to tell him the whole truth either. So there are cases where returning what you owe is the unjust thing to do, and the definition fails.
defs.re_zh: 假設一位朋友在神智清楚的時候把武器借給你，後來他發瘋了，回來向你討。誰都會說你不該還給他，也不該把全部實情告訴他。可見有些時候，歸還所欠的東西反而是不義的，這個定義不成立。

defs.en: Justice is doing good to your friends and harm to your enemies.
defs.zh: 正義就是對朋友行善、對敵人加害。
defs.flaw: Leads to absurdity · 推出荒謬
defs.re_en: We often misjudge people, and take the good for enemies and the bad for friends; then your justice would have us harm the good. And consider what harming does. A horse that is harmed becomes a worse horse, and a person who is harmed becomes worse in human excellence, that is, less just. Can it be the work of justice to make people unjust? Heat does not cool things, and the just person does not make anyone worse.
defs.re_zh: 我們常常看錯人，把好人當敵人、把壞人當朋友；那麼照你的正義，我們就該去傷害好人。再想想「加害」做了什麼：馬受了傷害，就成為一匹更差的馬；人受了傷害，在人的優秀品質上就變得更差，也就是更不正義。使人變得不正義，會是正義的工作嗎？熱不會使東西變冷，正義的人也不會使任何人變壞。

defs.en: Justice is nothing but the advantage of the stronger.
defs.zh: 正義不過是強者的利益。
defs.re_en: You say the rulers make laws for their own advantage, and that it is just for subjects to obey. But rulers are not infallible. Sometimes they mistake their own interest and command what harms them. On your account it is just to obey those commands too. So it is just to do what is to the advantage of the stronger, and also just to do what is to their disadvantage.
defs.re_zh: 你說統治者為了自己的利益立法，而臣民服從就是正義。可是統治者不是不會犯錯的。有時他們誤判自己的利益，下了對自己有害的命令。照你的說法，服從這些命令也是正義的。那麼，做對強者有利的事是正義，做對強者不利的事也是正義。

dialogues.end_en: Book I ends with Socrates admitting that he has feasted on arguments without ever settling what justice is. The other nine books of the Republic are his second attempt.
dialogues.end_zh: 第一卷結尾，蘇格拉底承認自己把論證嘗了個遍，卻始終沒有弄清楚正義是什麼。《理想國》其餘九卷，是他的第二次嘗試。

dialogues.who_en: Socrates, on his way to answer the charge of impiety, meets Euthyphro, who is prosecuting his own father for murder and is certain that this is the pious thing to do.
dialogues.who_zh: 蘇格拉底正要去應訊「不敬神」的指控，途中遇到歐緒弗洛。歐緒弗洛正要控告自己的父親殺人，而且確信這樣做才是虔敬。

defs.en: Piety is doing as I am doing: prosecuting the wrongdoer, whoever he may be.
defs.zh: 虔敬就是做我現在做的事：告發犯罪的人，不管他是誰。
defs.flaw: An example, not a definition · 是例子，不是定義
defs.re_en: I did not ask you for one or two of the many pious acts. I asked for the form itself that makes all pious acts pious, so that I can look to it as a standard and say of any act whether it is of that kind. You have told me that this is pious. You have not told me what piety is.
defs.re_zh: 我問的不是許多虔敬行為當中的一兩件。我問的是使一切虔敬行為成為虔敬的那個「形式」本身，好讓我拿它當標準，判斷任何一個行為屬不屬於這一類。你告訴了我「這件事是虔敬的」，還沒有告訴我「虔敬是什麼」。

defs.en: Piety is what is dear to the gods.
defs.re_en: By your own account the gods quarrel, and what they quarrel about is the just and the unjust, the good and the bad. Then the same act will be loved by some gods and hated by others, and it will be pious and impious at once. Your own prosecution may please Zeus and offend Cronos.
defs.re_zh: 照你自己的說法，諸神彼此爭吵，而他們爭的正是公不公正、善不善。那麼同一個行為會被某些神喜愛、被另一些神憎恨，它就同時是虔敬的又是不虔敬的。你這場告發，也許宙斯喜歡，克洛諾斯卻不高興。

defs.en: Piety is what all the gods love.
defs.zh: 虔敬就是所有的神都喜愛的。
defs.flaw: The Euthyphro dilemma · 歐緒弗洛兩難
defs.re_en: Is the pious loved by the gods because it is pious, or is it pious because it is loved by the gods? You say the first. But then being loved by the gods is something that happens to piety, a consequence of what it already is. You have told me a fact about piety and left its nature untouched. If you say the second, anything at all would become pious the moment the gods happened to love it.
defs.re_zh: 虔敬的事，是因為它虔敬所以被神喜愛，還是因為被神喜愛所以它虔敬？你說是前者。可是這樣一來，「被神喜愛」只是發生在虔敬身上的一件事，是它本來是什麼的結果。你告訴了我關於虔敬的一個事實，卻沒有碰到它的本質。如果你說是後者，那麼任何事情只要神碰巧喜愛，就立刻變成虔敬的了。

dialogues.end_en: Euthyphro says he is in a hurry and leaves. The question he could not answer, whether something is good because it is commanded or commanded because it is good, is still argued over in ethics and theology.
dialogues.end_zh: 歐緒弗洛說他趕時間，走了。他答不出來的那個問題——一件事是因為被命令所以善，還是因為善所以被命令——至今仍是倫理學與神學爭論的題目。

tests.en: Is it a definition, or only an example? A list of brave acts does not say what makes them brave.
tests.zh: 它是定義，還是只是例子？列出幾件勇敢的事，並沒有說出是什麼使它們勇敢。

tests.en: Is it too narrow? Look for a clear case of the thing that the definition leaves out.
tests.zh: 它是不是太窄？找一個明明屬於這個概念、卻被定義排除在外的例子。

tests.en: Is it too broad? Look for something the definition lets in that plainly does not belong.
tests.zh: 它是不是太寬？找一個明明不屬於這個概念、卻被定義放進來的例子。

tests.en: Is it circular? Check whether the word being defined, or a near synonym, has slipped into the definition.
tests.zh: 它是不是循環？檢查被定義的那個詞，或它的近義詞，有沒有溜進定義裡。

tests.en: Does it conflict with something else you believe? If it does, one of the two has to go.
tests.zh: 它跟你相信的別的事衝不衝突？如果衝突，兩者之中總得放棄一個。

lab.own_en: Now write your own definition of friendship, fairness, or respect, and run the five tests on it. Nothing you type leaves this page.
lab.own_zh: 現在換你：替「友誼」「公平」或「尊重」寫一個自己的定義，再用上面五個問題檢驗它。你輸入的內容不會離開這個頁面。

argument.lead_en: Why should anyone submit to this treatment? Socrates’ answer at his trial can be set out as an argument. Click a premise to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 為什麼要讓自己受這種詰問？蘇格拉底在法庭上的回答，可以攤開成一個論證。點任何一個前提，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: To live well, a person needs true beliefs about what matters: what is just, what is brave, what is good.
steps.zh: 要活得好，人需要對重要的事有正確的信念：什麼是正義、什麼是勇敢、什麼是善。
steps.ob_en: Rarely attacked. One could deny it by holding that living well is a matter of habit or good fortune, and that belief has little to do with it.
steps.ob_zh: 很少被攻擊。要否認它，可以主張活得好靠的是習慣或運氣，跟信念沒有多大關係。

steps.en: Most of our beliefs about these things were absorbed from family and city, and have never been tested. Untested beliefs may be false, or may contradict one another, without our noticing.
steps.zh: 我們對這些事的信念，多半是從家庭與城邦吸收來的，從來沒有受過檢驗。沒受過檢驗的信念可能是錯的，也可能互相矛盾，而我們自己不會發現。
steps.ob_en: The elenchus itself is the evidence for this premise: generals cannot define courage, and a religious expert cannot define piety.
steps.ob_zh: 詰問法本身就是這個前提的證據：將軍定義不出勇敢，宗教專家定義不出虔敬。

steps.en: The only way to find out which beliefs survive is to examine them: state them, give reasons, and face objections.
steps.zh: 要知道哪些信念站得住，唯一的辦法是省察它們：說出來、給理由、面對反駁。
steps.ob_en: A traditionalist may reply that long experience has already tested inherited beliefs, and tested them better than one person’s reasoning can. This is roughly Edmund Burke’s defense of “prejudice.”
steps.ob_zh: 傳統主義者可以回答：世代累積的經驗已經檢驗過這些繼承來的信念，而且比一個人的推理檢驗得更好。這大致是柏克為「成見」所做的辯護。

steps.en: Therefore a life without examination leaves living well to luck. In Socrates’ stronger words, it is “not worth living.”
steps.zh: 所以，不經省察的人生，把「活得好」交給了運氣。用蘇格拉底更重的話說，這樣的人生「不值得活」。
steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked. The premises support the weaker conclusion at most. Many people who never philosophize are kind, brave, and content, and it seems false, even arrogant, to say their lives are not worth living.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步。前提頂多支持那個比較弱的結論。許多從不做哲學思考的人善良、勇敢、知足；說他們的人生不值得活，似乎是錯的，甚至是傲慢的。

source.lead_en: The Apology is Plato’s version of the speech Socrates gave at his trial in 399 BCE. (Apologia means a defense in court; he apologizes for nothing.) Two short passages carry the lesson.
source.lead_zh: 《申辯篇》是柏拉圖筆下，蘇格拉底在西元前 399 年受審時的發言。（apologia 是法庭上的「辯護」，他什麼歉也沒道。）兩小段話就帶出了這一課的重點。

passages.en: Well, although I do not suppose that either of us knows anything really beautiful and good, I am better off than he is,—for he knows nothing, and thinks that he knows; I neither know nor think that I know. In this latter particular, then, I seem to have slightly the advantage of him.
passages.zh: 好吧，雖然我不認為我們兩人當中有誰真的知道什麼美與善的事，我還是比他好一點：他什麼都不知道，卻以為自己知道；我既不知道，也不以為自己知道。就在後面這一點上，我似乎比他略勝一籌。
passages.note_en: Notice how modest the claim is. He does not say “I know that I know nothing,” which would contradict itself. He says he does not think he knows what he does not know, and that this gives him a slight advantage.
passages.note_zh: 注意這個說法有多節制。他沒有說「我知道我一無所知」，那句話會自相矛盾。他說的是：我不知道的事，我不以為自己知道；而這只讓他「略勝一籌」。

passages.en: …and if I say again that daily to discourse about virtue, and of those other things about which you hear me examining myself and others, is the greatest good of man, and that the unexamined life is not worth living, you are still less likely to believe me.
passages.zh: ……如果我又說，每天談論德行，談論你們聽到我省察自己、也省察別人的那些事，是人最大的善；而未經省察的人生不值得活——你們就更不會相信我了。
passages.note_en: The famous line sits in a subordinate clause, inside a sentence about not being believed. He has just been found guilty and is explaining why he will not accept exile on condition of silence. Note also “examining myself and others”: the examination is turned on himself first.
passages.note_zh: 這句名言其實藏在一個子句裡，而整個句子講的是「你們不會相信我」。他剛被判有罪，正在解釋為什麼不接受「閉嘴就可以流亡」的條件。也注意「省察自己、也省察別人」：省察的對象，先是他自己。

items.o_en: Philosophy makes no progress. After twenty-five centuries philosophers still disagree about everything, while a first-year physics student knows more than Newton did.
items.o_zh: 哲學沒有進步。兩千五百年了，哲學家還是什麼都吵不出結論；而一個大一物理系學生知道的，已經比牛頓多。
items.r_en: Russell’s reply is that solved problems are renamed and leave the field, so what remains is always the unsolved part. A second reply is that progress in philosophy is often negative: we now know why a great many tempting answers fail, and that is knowledge. A critic may fairly press the point, however. If no positive answer has ever been secured, on what grounds do we call the activity a form of inquiry at all?
items.r_zh: 羅素的回答是：解決了的問題會改名、離開這個領域，所以留下來的永遠是沒解決的那一部分。第二個回答是，哲學的進步常常是否定式的：我們現在知道許多誘人的答案為什麼不成立，而這就是知識。不過批評者可以合理地追問下去：如果從來沒有一個正面的答案站穩過，我們憑什麼說這是一種「探究」？

items.o_en: The elenchus only destroys. Socrates refutes every answer and offers none, and his victims leave humiliated, having learned nothing.
items.o_zh: 詰問法只會破壞。蘇格拉底駁倒每一個答案，自己卻不給答案；被他問倒的人顏面盡失地離開，什麼也沒學到。
items.r_en: In the Meno, Socrates leads a boy to see that his confident answer to a geometry problem is wrong, and then asks whether the boy is worse off for it. Before, he thought he knew and would not have looked for the answer; now he knows that he does not know, and wants to find out (Meno 84a–c). Clearing away false confidence is the first step of learning. Whether Socrates took that step kindly is another matter, and Athens evidently thought he did not.
items.r_zh: 在《美諾篇》裡，蘇格拉底帶一個少年看出他對一道幾何題的自信答案是錯的，然後問：這個少年因此變糟了嗎？先前他以為自己知道，所以不會去找答案；現在他知道自己不知道，而且想弄清楚（《美諾篇》84a–c）。清掉虛假的自信，是學習的第一步。至於蘇格拉底做這一步的時候夠不夠厚道，那是另一回事；雅典人顯然認為他不夠。

items.o_en: “The unexamined life is not worth living” is elitist. It condemns most of the human beings who have ever lived.
items.o_zh: 「未經省察的人生不值得活」是菁英主義，它等於否定了有史以來絕大多數人的人生。
items.r_en: One defense reads the line narrowly: Socrates is speaking of himself, explaining why he could not live silenced. Another reads “examined” modestly, as the ordinary practice of asking whether you are living as you think you should, which requires no schooling. On either reading the claim is easier to defend than the slogan suggests. Read at full strength, as a verdict on other people’s lives, it is very hard to defend.
items.r_zh: 一種辯護把這句話讀得很窄：蘇格拉底是在說他自己，在解釋為什麼他沒辦法閉著嘴活下去。另一種辯護把「省察」讀得很平實：就是平常問問自己，是不是照著自己認為應該的方式在活；這不需要讀過書。照這兩種讀法，這個主張都比那句口號容易辯護。但如果照字面的全部力道，把它讀成對別人人生的判決，就很難辯護了。

said.en: This sentence appears nowhere in Plato. It is a later compression of Apology 21d, where Socrates says only that he does not think he knows what he does not know. The compressed version is also self-defeating, since it claims to know something. The Latin tag often quoted for it, scio me nihil scire, is likewise a later formulation.
said.zh: 柏拉圖的著作裡找不到這句話。它是後人把《申辯篇》21d 濃縮而成的；蘇格拉底在那裡只說，他不知道的事，他不以為自己知道。濃縮版還會自打嘴巴，因為它宣稱「知道」了一件事。常被引用的拉丁文版本 scio me nihil scire，同樣是後來才有的說法。

terms.d_en: The examination, by argument, of basic questions about knowledge, reality, and value.
terms.d_zh: 以論證的方式，檢驗關於知識、真實與價值的基本問題。

terms.d_en: Socrates’ method: draw out a definition, then show that it conflicts with other things the speaker believes.
terms.d_zh: 蘇格拉底的方法：引出一個定義，再指出它跟說話者相信的其他事互相衝突。

terms.d_en: The state of being at a loss when every proposed answer has failed.
terms.d_zh: 所有提出的答案都失敗之後，那種不知所措的狀態。

terms.d_en: The branch that studies knowledge, belief, and justification.
terms.d_zh: 研究知識、信念與證成的分支。

terms.o: Gk. ta meta ta physika, ‘the books after the Physics’
terms.d_en: The branch that studies what exists and its most general features. The name began as a librarian’s label for where Aristotle’s treatise was shelved.
terms.d_zh: 研究什麼存在、以及存在物最普遍特徵的分支。這個名字原本只是圖書編目的標籤，指亞里斯多德那部書排在《物理學》之後。

terms.d_en: The branch that studies how one ought to live and act.
terms.d_zh: 研究人應該怎麼生活、怎麼行動的分支。

terms.d_en: A set of premises offered in support of a conclusion. In philosophy the word never means a quarrel.
terms.d_zh: 用來支持一個結論的一組前提。在哲學裡，這個字從來不是「吵架」的意思。

terms.d_en: A single case that shows a general claim to be false.
terms.d_zh: 足以證明一個普遍主張為假的單一個案。

vocab.eg: No further observation would settle a question like that.
vocab.eg_zh: 再多觀察也解決不了這種問題。

vocab.eg: An ancient story credits the word to Pythagoras.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個古老的故事把這個字歸給畢達哥拉斯。

vocab.eg: Something you took to be obvious does not, on inspection, make sense.
vocab.eg_zh: 你以為理所當然的事，仔細一看竟說不通。

vocab.eg: Aporia is a state of being at a loss.
vocab.eg_zh: Aporia 是一種不知所措的狀態。

vocab.eg: Philosophy accepts no conclusion on authority.
vocab.eg_zh: 哲學不憑權威接受任何結論。

vocab.eg: The borders between the branches are porous.
vocab.eg_zh: 各分支之間的邊界並不嚴密。

vocab.eg: The term was coined only in 1874.
vocab.eg_zh: 這個詞直到 1874 年才被造出來。

vocab.eg: What remains under the old name is the unfinished business.
vocab.eg_zh: 留在舊名字底下的，是還沒做完的事。

vocab.zh: 為了它本身（而非別的目的）
vocab.eg: The unfinished business is worth doing for its own sake.
vocab.eg_zh: 這些沒做完的事，本身就值得做。

vocab.eg: A mind that has never doubted its assumptions is confined by them.
vocab.eg_zh: 從未懷疑過自己預設的心靈，就被這些預設關住了。

quiz.q: According to the essay, what distinguishes the “second wall” from the first?
options: No further observation could settle the question.
The answer exists, but only experts know it.
The question is asked by a child.
The question concerns religion.

quiz.q: Why does Socrates regard aporia as a gain?
options: Someone who knows that he does not know is in a position to start looking.
It proves that definitions are impossible.
It shows that the other speaker is a fool.
It ends the conversation quickly.

quiz.q: What is wrong with Euthyphro’s first answer, “piety is doing as I am doing”?
options: It gives an example where a definition was asked for.
It is circular.
It contradicts what the gods have said.
It is too broad.

quiz.q: Which statement best matches Apology 21d?
options: I do not think I know what I do not know.
I know that I know nothing.
No one can know anything.
I am the wisest man in Athens.

quiz.q: What is Russell’s first reply to the charge that philosophy settles nothing?
options: Questions that become answerable are renamed as sciences and leave philosophy.
Philosophy has in fact settled most of its questions.
Definite answers do not matter to anyone.
Science has not settled anything either.

write.en: Pick a word you use every day (friend, fair, success) and write a one-sentence definition. Then write the strongest counterexample you can find, and revise the definition once.
write.zh: 選一個你天天在用的詞（朋友、公平、成功），用一句話下定義。接著寫出你想得到的最強反例，再把定義修改一次。

write.en: Is the unexamined life really “not worth living”? Defend either the strong claim or the weaker one in about 150 words, and answer one objection.
write.zh: 未經省察的人生真的「不值得活」嗎？用大約 150 個英文字，為強的主張或弱的主張辯護，並回應一個反駁。

write.en: Russell says that solved philosophical problems are renamed as sciences. Name one question that you think will never make that move, and say why.
write.zh: 羅素說，解決了的哲學問題會改名成為科學。舉出一個你認為永遠不會「搬家」的問題，並說明理由。

paras.en: The Buddha was also a master of the question. An early discourse (Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.42) sorts questions into four kinds: those to be answered directly, those to be answered after drawing distinctions, those to be answered with a counter-question, and those to be set aside. The third kind is what Socrates did for a living, and the second, vibhajja, “analysis,” gave one early school its name.
paras.zh: 佛陀也是提問的大師。早期的一部經（《增支部》4.42）把問題分成四種：應當直接回答的（一向記）、應當分別之後再回答的（分別記）、應當反問之後再回答的（反詰記）、應當擱置不答的（捨置記）。第三種正是蘇格拉底終身在做的事；第二種「分別」（vibhajja），後來成了早期一個部派的名字。

paras.en: The fourth kind marks the real difference. Socrates held that examination is itself the good life, and he pursued a question wherever it led. The Buddha set certain questions aside, among them whether the world is eternal and whether it is finite, on the ground that pursuing them does not lead to the end of suffering. For him, inquiry is governed by a practical aim. Whether that restriction is a limit on philosophy or a philosophical position in its own right is a question this series will return to (Dharma and the West, D21).
paras.zh: 第四種才是真正的差別所在。蘇格拉底認為省察本身就是美好的人生，問題走到哪裡他就追到哪裡。佛陀則把某些問題擱在一邊，例如世界是不是永恆、是不是有邊，理由是追究這些問題並不導向苦的止息。對佛陀來說，探究受一個實踐目的節制。這個限制到底是對哲學的限縮，還是本身就是一種哲學立場？這個系列之後會回來談（佛法與西方哲學 D21）。

lessons.title: What Makes a Good Argument?
lessons.blurb_en: Validity, soundness, and the discovery that the shape of an argument can be judged apart from what it is about.
lessons.blurb_zh: 有效、健全，以及一個發現：論證的形狀，可以跟它在談什麼分開來評判。
lessons.big_en: A good deductive argument does two separate jobs: its conclusion follows from its premises, and its premises are true. Logic can check the first without knowing anything about the second.
lessons.big_zh: 一個好的演繹論證要做到兩件各自獨立的事：結論從前提推得出來，而且前提是真的。邏輯可以檢查第一件，而完全不必知道第二件。

paras.en: In ordinary speech an argument is a quarrel. In philosophy it is something quieter and more useful: a set of statements, the premises, offered as reasons for accepting another statement, the conclusion. To give an argument is to put your reasons on the table where other people can inspect them. There are then exactly two ways it can fail. One or more of the premises may be false, or the conclusion may not follow from the premises even if they are all true. The whole of logic grows out of keeping these two failures apart.
paras.zh: 在日常用語裡，argument 是吵架。在哲學裡，它安靜得多，也有用得多：一組陳述（前提）被提出來，當作接受另一個陳述（結論）的理由。提出論證，就是把你的理由攤在桌上，讓別人檢查。這樣一來，它失敗的方式恰好只有兩種：前提當中有一個或幾個是假的；或者，就算前提全是真的，結論也推不出來。整門邏輯學，都是從把這兩種失敗分開而長出來的。

paras.en: Take the most famous example in the subject. All humans are mortal; Socrates is human; therefore Socrates is mortal. If you grant the two premises you cannot consistently deny the conclusion. An argument with this property is called valid: it is impossible for all of its premises to be true while its conclusion is false. The premises are then said to entail the conclusion.
paras.zh: 拿這門學問裡最有名的例子來看。所有人都會死；蘇格拉底是人；所以蘇格拉底會死。如果你承認這兩個前提，就不可能不自相矛盾地否認結論。有這種性質的論證叫作「有效」：它的前提不可能全部為真而結論為假。這時我們說，前提「蘊涵」結論。

paras.en: Aristotle (384–322 BCE) saw that this necessity has nothing to do with Socrates or with death. It holds by virtue of the pattern alone. Replace the terms with letters, as he was the first to do, and the pattern still compels: if A belongs to every B, and B belongs to every C, then A belongs to every C. Whatever you put in for the letters, true premises will never lead to a false conclusion. With that step, the study of reasoning became a science of forms.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德（西元前 384–322 年）看出，這種必然性跟蘇格拉底無關，也跟死亡無關；它單單憑著那個樣式成立。像他首創的那樣，把詞項換成字母，這個樣式照樣有約束力：如果 A 屬於每一個 B，而 B 屬於每一個 C，那麼 A 屬於每一個 C。不管你把什麼填進字母裡，真的前提永遠不會導出假的結論。跨出這一步，對推理的研究就成了一門關於形式的科學。

paras.en: The definition has a consequence that surprises almost everyone at first. Validity says nothing about whether the premises are in fact true. “All fish can fly; all whales are fish; therefore all whales can fly” is a perfectly valid argument. Every statement in it is false, and yet the conclusion follows: if the premises were true, the conclusion would have to be.
paras.zh: 這個定義有一個後果，幾乎每個人初次聽到都會吃驚：有效性完全不管前提事實上是不是真的。「所有的魚都會飛；所有的鯨都是魚；所以所有的鯨都會飛」是一個完全有效的論證。裡面每一句都是假的，可是結論推得出來：假如前提為真，結論就非真不可。

paras.en: The reverse also happens. “All poets are human; Li Bai is human; therefore Li Bai is a poet” has two true premises and a true conclusion, and it is invalid. The quickest way to see this is to keep the form and change the content: all poets are human; Socrates is human; therefore Socrates is a poet. The premises are still true and the conclusion is now false, so the form cannot be trusted, and it never could. This is the method of counterexample, and it is the logician’s basic instrument.
paras.zh: 反過來的情況也有。「所有詩人都是人；李白是人；所以李白是詩人」有兩個真前提、一個真結論，卻是無效的。要看出這一點，最快的辦法是保留形式、更換內容：所有詩人都是人；蘇格拉底是人；所以蘇格拉底是詩人。前提還是真的，結論卻變成假的了，可見這個形式靠不住，而且從來就靠不住。這就是反例法，邏輯學家最基本的工具。

paras.en: An argument that is valid and also has true premises is called sound. Soundness is what we actually want, because only a sound argument guarantees its conclusion. The division of labor is worth noticing. Whether an argument is valid can be settled from an armchair. Whether its premises are true usually cannot: that depends on biology, or history, or whatever else the premises bear on. Logic transmits truth from premises to conclusion. It does not supply the truth in the first place.
paras.zh: 既有效、前提又都為真的論證，叫作「健全」。健全才是我們真正要的，因為只有健全的論證保證它的結論。這裡的分工值得留意。一個論證有沒有效，坐在扶手椅上就能判定。它的前提是不是真的，通常不行：那要看生物學、歷史，或前提所涉及的任何別的領域。邏輯把真從前提傳送到結論；它並不一開始就供應真。

essay.h_en: Four patterns worth knowing by name
essay.h_zh: 四個值得記住名字的樣式

paras.en: Much everyday reasoning runs on “if.” Two patterns are valid. Modus ponens: if P then Q; P; therefore Q. Modus tollens: if P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. Each has an invalid twin that looks almost the same. Affirming the consequent: if it rained, the street is wet; the street is wet; therefore it rained. (A street cleaner may have passed.) Denying the antecedent: if it rained, the street is wet; it did not rain; therefore the street is not wet. A wet street does not rule out other causes, and that is all it takes for both twins to fail.
paras.zh: 日常推理有一大半是靠「如果」在運轉的。有兩個樣式有效。肯定前件（modus ponens）：如果 P 則 Q；P；所以 Q。否定後件（modus tollens）：如果 P 則 Q；非 Q；所以非 P。它們各有一個長得幾乎一樣的無效雙胞胎。肯定後件：如果下過雨，街道是溼的；街道是溼的；所以下過雨。（也許是洗街車剛經過。）否定前件：如果下過雨，街道是溼的；沒下過雨；所以街道不是溼的。街道溼，並不排除別的原因；單憑這一點，兩個雙胞胎就都不成立。

essay.h_en: When the conclusion goes beyond the premises

paras.en: Everything so far concerns deduction, where the premises are meant to guarantee the conclusion. Most reasoning in science and in life is of another kind. From “every swan observed so far has been white” to “all swans are white” is an inductive step: the conclusion says more than the premises do, and so it can be false even when they are true. Inductive arguments are therefore never valid, and it would be a mistake to blame them for that. They are judged by strength, and a strong one makes its conclusion probable. Whether that standard can itself be justified is a famous problem, taken up in lesson A8.
paras.zh: 到目前為止談的都是演繹：前提要保證結論。科學與生活裡的推理，大半屬於另一種。從「目前觀察到的每一隻天鵝都是白的」到「所有天鵝都是白的」是歸納的一步：結論說的比前提多，所以即使前提為真，結論也可能為假。因此歸納論證永遠不是有效的，而為此責怪它是弄錯了對象。評判它的標準是「強度」：強的歸納論證使結論很可能為真。這個標準本身能不能被證成，是一個著名的難題，留到 A8 那一課。

paras.en: Logic was invented at least three times. In China the later Mohists, in the third century BCE, analyzed disputation and held that an explanation must bring out the reason for a claim: 以說出故. In India the Nyāya school set out a five-step inference that became the common property of Hindu and Buddhist philosophers: the hill has fire; because it has smoke; wherever there is smoke there is fire, as in a kitchen; this hill has smoke; therefore it has fire.
paras.zh: 邏輯至少被發明過三次。在中國，西元前三世紀的後期墨家分析了辯論，主張解說必須把一個主張的理由提出來：「以說出故」。在印度，正理派定出了五支的推論，後來成為印度教與佛教哲學家的共同資產：此山有火；因為有煙；凡有煙處必有火，如廚房；此山有煙；所以此山有火。

paras.en: The Indian pattern differs from Aristotle’s in one instructive way. It insists on an example, the kitchen, so that the general rule is tied to a case both parties have seen. A Greek syllogism asks only whether the conclusion follows. An Indian inference asks in addition how the rule is known. That second question, as we shall see, is exactly where Aristotle’s critics attacked.
paras.zh: 印度的樣式跟亞里斯多德的有一個很有啟發性的差別：它堅持要舉一個例子（廚房），把普遍規則繫在雙方都見過的個案上。希臘的三段論只問結論推不推得出來；印度的推論還多問一句：這條規則是怎麼知道的？我們接下來會看到，批評亞里斯多德的人，攻擊的正是這第二個問題。

paras.en: It may seem that validity is trivially easy to get, and in a sense it is: for any conclusion at all, one can invent premises that entail it. That is why a valid argument settles nothing by itself, and why serious disagreement is nearly always about premises. Yet the discipline of form is what makes such disagreement productive. Set an opponent’s reasoning out in valid form, supplying in its strongest version whatever was left unsaid, and you will see which premise carries the weight. You then know precisely what the two of you disagree about, and in turn what evidence would bear on it. Philosophers call this the principle of charity. It is good manners, and it is also the fastest way to find out who is right.
paras.zh: 有效性似乎輕而易舉就能到手；在某個意義上確實如此：不管什麼結論，都可以編出蘊涵它的前提。正因為這樣，一個有效的論證本身什麼也沒解決，而認真的分歧幾乎總是關於前提的。可是，讓這種分歧有成果的，正是對形式的講究。把對手的推理整理成有效的形式，沒說出口的部分用最強的版本替他補上，你就會看出是哪一個前提在承重。這時你確切知道你們兩人到底在爭什麼，進而知道什麼證據跟它有關。哲學家稱之為「善意理解原則」。這是好的風度，同時也是找出誰對的最快方法。

lab.title_en: Try it: valid, sound, or neither?
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：有效、健全，還是都不是？
lab.lead_en: Six short arguments. For each, decide first whether the conclusion follows. Only if it does is there a second question: are the premises all true? Do not let a true conclusion, or a false one, make the decision for you.
lab.lead_zh: 六個短論證。每一個先判斷結論推不推得出來；推得出來，才有第二個問題：前提全是真的嗎？別讓結論的真假替你做決定。

why.en: The form guarantees the conclusion, and both premises are true. This is what a sound argument looks like.
why.zh: 形式保證了結論，兩個前提又都是真的。健全的論證就是這個樣子。

why.en: Same form as the first argument, so it is valid: if the premises were true, the conclusion would have to be. Both premises are false, so it is unsound. Validity does not care.
why.zh: 形式跟第一個論證相同，所以有效：假如前提為真，結論就非真不可。兩個前提都是假的，所以不健全。有效性不在乎這個。

why.en: Everything here is true, and the argument is still invalid. The premises put poets inside the class of humans and Li Bai inside it too, and say nothing about how the two are related.
why.zh: 這裡每一句都是真的，論證卻仍然無效。前提把詩人放進「人」這個類，也把李白放進去，但對這兩者的關係什麼都沒說。

counter.en: All poets are human. Socrates is human. Therefore Socrates is a poet.
counter.zh: 所有詩人都是人。蘇格拉底是人。所以蘇格拉底是詩人。

p.en: If it rained last night, the street is wet.
p.zh: 如果昨晚下過雨，街道是溼的。

why.en: The first premise says rain is enough for a wet street. It does not say rain is the only way. This is how a detective’s guess differs from a proof.
why.zh: 第一個前提說下雨足以讓街道溼，並沒有說那是唯一的方式。偵探的猜測與證明，差別就在這裡。

counter.en: If I am in Taipei, I am in Taiwan. I am in Taiwan. Therefore I am in Taipei.
counter.zh: 如果我在臺北，我就在臺灣。我在臺灣。所以我在臺北。

p.en: If the Buddha was born in Athens, he was born in Greece.
p.zh: 如果佛陀生於雅典，他就生於希臘。

p.en: The Buddha was not born in Greece.

c.en: The Buddha was not born in Athens.

why.en: Modus tollens. Note that the first premise is true although both of its parts are false: a conditional claims only a connection.
why.zh: 否定後件。注意第一個前提是真的，雖然它的兩個部分都是假的：條件句只宣稱一個連結。

why.en: Valid, with one false premise. Because the form is valid and the conclusion is false, we can run the argument backward: at least one premise must be false. This is how a valid argument is used to refute.
why.zh: 有效，但有一個假前提。因為形式有效而結論為假，我們可以把論證倒過來用：至少有一個前提是假的。有效論證就是這樣被用來反駁的。

table: Sound: the conclusion must be true
Unsound: the conclusion may be true or false
Unsound: the conclusion may be true or false
Unsound: the conclusion may be true or false

argument.lead_en: The most serious attack on the syllogism is itself an argument, and John Stuart Mill gave it its classic form in 1843. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 對三段論最嚴重的攻擊，本身也是一個論證；彌爾在 1843 年給了它經典的形式。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: We are entitled to assert “All men are mortal” only if we already know, of each man, that he is mortal.
steps.zh: 我們有資格斷言「所有人都會死」，唯有在我們已經知道每一個人都會死的時候。
steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked. We do not learn general truths by checking every case. We infer them from observed cases, or accept them as laws, and then apply them to cases we have never examined.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步。我們不是靠逐一檢查每個個案來得知普遍真理的。我們從觀察過的個案推出它，或把它當作定律接受，再應用到從沒檢查過的個案上。

steps.en: Socrates is one of the men. So knowing the first premise already includes knowing that Socrates is mortal.
steps.zh: 蘇格拉底是其中一個人。所以知道第一個前提，已經包含了知道蘇格拉底會死。
steps.ob_en: This follows only if P1 is granted. Someone can know the rule without having considered this instance, as a doctor knows that a drug is toxic before meeting the next patient.
steps.ob_zh: 只有承認了 P1，這一步才成立。一個人可以知道規則，而沒有考慮過這個個例；就像醫生在見到下一位病人之前，就知道某種藥有毒。

steps.en: An argument whose premises already assume its conclusion proves nothing. It begs the question.
steps.zh: 前提已經預設了結論的論證，什麼也沒證明。它犯了「乞題」。
steps.ob_en: True of circular arguments. But in every valid argument the conclusion is, in a logical sense, contained in the premises; that is what validity means. If containment were a fault, all deduction would be worthless, including geometry.
steps.ob_zh: 對循環論證來說確實如此。可是每一個有效論證，結論在邏輯上都「包含」在前提裡；有效性本來就是這個意思。如果包含是毛病，一切演繹就都沒有價值了，連幾何學也是。

steps.en: Therefore the syllogism, taken as a proof of its conclusion, is circular.
steps.zh: 所以，三段論若被當成對其結論的證明，是循環的。
steps.ob_en: Mill accepted this conclusion and drew a striking moral: real inference runs from particular cases to particular cases, and the general premise is only a memorandum of what we have observed. Most later logicians rejected P1 and kept the syllogism.
steps.ob_zh: 彌爾接受這個結論，並且引出一個驚人的教訓：真正的推論是從個案到個案，普遍前提只是我們觀察所得的備忘錄。後來大多數邏輯學家否定 P1，保住了三段論。

source.work_zh: 亞里斯多德《前分析篇》卷一第一至四章
source.tr: translated by A. J. Jenkinson (public domain)
source.lead_en: The Prior Analytics is the first treatise on formal logic in any language. It opens by saying what a deduction is; three chapters later, letters replace words.
source.lead_zh: 《前分析篇》是任何語言裡第一部形式邏輯的專論。它開頭先說明什麼是演繹；三章之後，字母取代了詞語。

passages.en: A syllogism is discourse in which, certain things being stated, something other than what is stated follows of necessity from their being so.
passages.zh: 三段論是這樣一種論述：某些事情被陳述了之後，另一件不同於所陳述的事情，因為它們如此而必然隨之而來。
passages.note_en: Three phrases carry the definition. “Certain things”: more than one premise. “Something other”: the conclusion must be new, which rules out merely repeating a premise. “Of necessity”: this is the first statement of what we now call validity. Syllogismos here means deduction in general, a wider sense than the three-line pattern the word later came to name.
passages.note_zh: 三個詞組撐起這個定義。「某些事情」：前提不只一個。「另一件不同的事」：結論必須是新的，這就排除了單純重複前提。「必然」：這是我們今天所說的「有效性」最早的表述。這裡的 syllogismos 指的是一般的演繹，比後來專指三行格式的那個意思要寬。

passages.en: If A is predicated of all B, and B of all C, A must be predicated of all C.
passages.zh: 如果 A 述說一切 B，而 B 述說一切 C，那麼 A 必定述說一切 C。
passages.note_en: This plain sentence is one of the great inventions. By writing A, B, and C, Aristotle shows that he is talking about every argument of this shape at once. Variables entered logic here, well before they were used in algebra. Notice also the order: he says “A of all B” where we say “all B are A,” which is why his syllogisms read backward to a modern eye.
passages.note_zh: 這個平淡的句子是偉大的發明之一。亞里斯多德寫下 A、B、C，表示他談的是所有這個形狀的論證。變項是從這裡進入邏輯的，遠早於代數使用它們。也注意語序：他說「A 述說一切 B」，我們說「所有 B 都是 A」；所以他的三段論在現代人看來是倒著寫的。

items.o_en: Deduction can never teach us anything. If the conclusion is already contained in the premises, a valid argument only tells us what we knew.
items.o_zh: 演繹永遠不能教我們任何東西。如果結論已經包含在前提裡，有效論證只是把我們已經知道的事再說一遍。
items.r_en: Logical containment is not psychological possession. The axioms of geometry contain the Pythagorean theorem, and no one who learns the axioms thereby knows the theorem. Deduction is informative for limited minds, and ours are limited. How an inference can be both necessary and informative is nevertheless a real puzzle, sometimes called the scandal of deduction.
items.r_zh: 邏輯上的包含，不等於心理上的擁有。幾何學的公理包含了畢氏定理，但沒有人學了公理就因此知道那條定理。對有限的心靈來說，演繹帶來新知，而我們的心靈是有限的。不過，一個推論怎麼能既是必然的、又帶來新知，確實是個難題，有人稱之為「演繹的醜聞」。

items.o_en: The rules of logic cannot be justified without using them. Any proof that modus ponens is reliable will rely on modus ponens.
items.o_zh: 邏輯規則沒辦法不靠它們自己來證成。任何證明「肯定前件」可靠的證明，都會用到肯定前件。
items.r_en: Lewis Carroll dramatized this in 1895. His Tortoise accepts the premises of a valid argument and refuses the conclusion until the rule of inference is written down as a further premise, and then asks for another, without end. The usual moral is that a rule of inference is not one more premise. It is something we do with premises, and at some point one must simply reason. Whether that amounts to a justification or to an admission that there is none is still argued.
items.r_zh: 路易斯・卡羅在 1895 年把這個問題寫成了一場戲。他筆下的烏龜接受一個有效論證的前提，卻不肯接受結論，除非先把推論規則寫下來當作又一個前提；寫下來之後，牠又要求再一個，沒完沒了。通常引出的教訓是：推論規則不是多一個前提，它是我們拿前提來「做」的事，到了某一點人就是得動手推理。這究竟算是一種證成，還是承認沒有證成，至今仍有爭論。

items.o_en: Validity is beside the point. People are not moved by syllogisms, and the arguments that matter in life are never deductive.
items.o_zh: 有效性根本不是重點。人不會被三段論打動，而人生中重要的論證從來不是演繹的。
items.r_en: The second half is nearly right: most reasoning that matters is inductive or practical. But the deductive standard still does work there. It lets us ask what would have to be added to make an argument valid, and the added premise is usually the one worth fighting about. As for persuasion, logic was never offered as a description of how people are moved. It describes what they would be right to be moved by.
items.r_zh: 後半句幾乎是對的：重要的推理大半是歸納的或實踐的。但演繹的標準在那裡仍然派得上用場。它讓我們問：要補上什麼，這個論證才會有效？而被補上的那個前提，通常就是最值得爭的那一個。至於說服力，邏輯從來不是要描述人實際上被什麼打動，它描述的是人被什麼打動才是對的。

said.claim: “All men are mortal; Socrates is a man; therefore Socrates is mortal.”
said.claim_zh: 「所有人都會死；蘇格拉底是人；所以蘇格拉底會死。」
said.verdict_zh: 亞里斯多德沒有這樣寫
said.en: The world’s best-known syllogism appears nowhere in Aristotle’s logical works. He stated his patterns with letters and seldom used a named individual as a term. The Socrates example is a schoolroom tradition of much later date; by 1843 Mill could treat it as the standard specimen. It is still a fair illustration of the pattern Aristotle discovered.
said.zh: 全世界最有名的三段論，在亞里斯多德的邏輯著作裡找不到。他用字母陳述他的樣式，很少拿一個有名有姓的個人當詞項。蘇格拉底這個例子是很久以後才有的課堂傳統；到了 1843 年，彌爾已經把它當成標準範例。用它來說明亞里斯多德發現的那個樣式，仍然是恰當的。

terms.d_en: A statement offered as a reason for the conclusion.
terms.d_zh: 被提出來當作結論之理由的陳述。

terms.d_en: Such that the premises cannot all be true while the conclusion is false. Said of arguments, never of statements.
terms.d_zh: 前提不可能全真而結論為假。只用來形容論證，不用來形容陳述。

terms.d_en: Valid, and with premises that are all true.
terms.d_zh: 有效，而且前提全部為真。

terms.d_en: Premises entail a conclusion when it follows from them necessarily.
terms.d_zh: 結論必然從前提推出時，我們說前提蘊涵結論。

terms.d_en: In Aristotle, any deduction; later, an argument with two premises and three terms.
terms.d_zh: 在亞里斯多德是任何演繹；後來專指兩個前提、三個詞項的論證。

terms.o: L. deducere ‘to lead down’; inducere ‘to lead in’
terms.d_en: Reasoning whose premises are meant to guarantee the conclusion; reasoning whose premises are meant to make it probable.
terms.d_zh: 前提要保證結論的推理；前提要使結論很可能為真的推理。

terms.d_en: If P then Q; P; therefore Q.
terms.d_zh: 如果 P 則 Q；P；所以 Q。

terms.d_en: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P.
terms.d_zh: 如果 P 則 Q；非 Q；所以非 P。

terms.d_en: Assuming in the premises the very thing to be proved.
terms.d_zh: 在前提裡預設了正要證明的那件事。

vocab.eg: If you grant the two premises you cannot consistently deny the conclusion.
vocab.eg_zh: 如果你承認這兩個前提，就不可能不自相矛盾地否認結論。

vocab.eg: It holds by virtue of the pattern alone.
vocab.eg_zh: 它單單憑著那個樣式成立。

vocab.eg: The necessity holds whatever the argument is about.
vocab.eg_zh: 不管論證在談什麼，這個必然性都成立。

vocab.eg: Replace the terms with letters and the pattern still compels.
vocab.eg_zh: 把詞項換成字母，這個樣式照樣有約束力。

vocab.zh: 不靠實地調查、光憑思考
vocab.eg: Whether an argument is valid can be settled from an armchair.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個論證有沒有效，坐在扶手椅上就能判定。

vocab.eg: That depends on whatever the premises bear on.
vocab.eg_zh: 那要看前提所涉及的是什麼。

vocab.eg: A wet street does not rule out other causes.
vocab.eg_zh: 街道溼，並不排除別的原因。

vocab.eg: Validity may seem trivially easy to get.
vocab.eg_zh: 有效性似乎輕而易舉就能到手。

vocab.eg: You know what you disagree about, and in turn what evidence would bear on it.
vocab.eg_zh: 你知道你們在爭什麼，進而知道什麼證據跟它有關。

vocab.zh: 乞題（預設了待證的結論）
vocab.eg: An argument whose premises assume its conclusion begs the question.
vocab.eg_zh: 前提預設了結論的論證，犯了乞題。

quiz.q: What does it mean to call an argument valid?
options: Its premises cannot all be true while its conclusion is false.
Its premises and conclusion are all true.
Most people find it convincing.
Its conclusion is probably true.

quiz.q: “All poets are human; Li Bai is human; therefore Li Bai is a poet.” What is wrong with it?
options: Nothing in it is false, but the conclusion does not follow.
The first premise is false.
The conclusion is false.
It is valid but unsound.

quiz.q: How does the method of counterexample show that a form is invalid?
options: It finds an argument of the same form with true premises and a false conclusion.
It shows that one premise is false.
It shows that the conclusion is unpopular.
It replaces the conclusion with its opposite.

quiz.q: According to the essay, how does the Indian five-step inference differ from Aristotle’s syllogism?
options: It requires an example that ties the general rule to a familiar case.
It has no conclusion.
It uses letters in place of words.
It rejects general rules.

quiz.q: Which premise of Mill’s objection do most later logicians reject?
options: That we can assert a general statement only after knowing every case.
That Socrates is a man.
That circular arguments prove nothing.
That all men are mortal.

write.en: Find a short argument in today’s news or in an advertisement. Set it out as numbered premises and a conclusion, supplying any premise that was left unsaid. Is it valid? Which premise would you challenge?
write.zh: 從今天的新聞或一則廣告裡找一個短論證。把它整理成編號的前提與結論，沒說出口的前提替它補上。它有效嗎？你會質疑哪一個前提？

write.en: Write one argument that is valid and plainly unsound, and one that is invalid although every statement in it is true. Then give a counterexample to the second.
write.zh: 寫一個有效但明顯不健全的論證，再寫一個每一句都是真的、卻無效的論證。然後替第二個找一個反例。

write.en: Is Mill right that the syllogism begs the question? Defend your answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 彌爾說三段論犯了乞題，他對嗎？用大約 150 個英文字為你的答案辯護。

paras.en: Buddhist philosophers had a logic of their own, hetuvidyā, the “science of reasons,” known in Chinese as 因明. Around 500 CE the logician Dignāga reduced the Nyāya’s five steps to three. Thesis: sound is impermanent. Reason: because it is produced. Example: whatever is produced is impermanent, like a pot; and nothing permanent is produced, like space.
paras.zh: 佛教哲學家有自己的邏輯：hetuvidyā，「關於理由的學問」，漢譯「因明」。大約西元 500 年，邏輯學家陳那把正理派的五支簡化成三支。宗：聲是無常。因：所作性故（因為它是造作出來的）。喻：凡所作者皆是無常，如瓶（同喻）；凡是常者皆非所作，如虛空（異喻）。

paras.en: Set beside Aristotle’s syllogism, the form is close: the example states the general rule, the reason applies it, and the thesis follows. The difference is the pot. A Buddhist inference is incomplete until the rule has been tied to a case that both parties accept, and tested against a contrasting case. Mill complained that the syllogism never tells us how its general premise is known. The Indian logicians had built an answer to that complaint into the form itself, some thirteen centuries earlier. Whether an example can really support a universal rule is, of course, the problem of induction again (Dharma and the West, D14).
paras.zh: 跟亞里斯多德的三段論擺在一起，形式很接近：喻陳述普遍規則，因把它應用上去，宗就隨之成立。差別在那只瓶子。佛教的推論要等到規則繫在雙方都接受的個案上，並且用一個相反的個案檢驗過，才算完整。彌爾抱怨三段論從不告訴我們，它的普遍前提是怎麼知道的。印度的邏輯學家早了大約一千三百年，就把對這個抱怨的回答做進了形式本身。當然，一個例子到底能不能支持一條普遍規則，那又是歸納問題了（佛法與西方哲學 D14）。

further.t: Aristotle, Prior Analytics, translated by A. J. Jenkinson
further.n_en: Book I, chapters 1 to 7, is enough to see the system being built.
further.n_zh: 讀卷一第一到七章，就足以看到這套系統怎麼搭起來。

further.t: John Stuart Mill, A System of Logic (1843), Book II, chapter 3
further.n_en: The charge that every syllogism begs the question. Public domain.
further.n_zh: 「每個三段論都犯了乞題」這項指控的出處。公版。

further.t: Lewis Carroll, “What the Tortoise Said to Achilles,” Mind (1895)
further.n_zh: 三頁，至今仍然令人不安。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Aristotle’s Logic”
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Logic and Language in Early Chinese Philosophy” and “Dignāga”

lessons.title: How Do Arguments Go Wrong?
lessons.blurb_en: Fallacies: arguments that look better than they are, why they work on us, and how to name one without committing another.
lessons.blurb_zh: 謬誤：看起來比實際上好的論證。它們為什麼對我們有效，以及怎樣指出一個謬誤，而自己不犯另一個。
lessons.big_en: A fallacy is a bad argument in good clothing. Each of the classic ones borrows the look of a pattern that is often reasonable, which is why learning their names matters less than seeing what each one imitates.
lessons.big_zh: 謬誤是穿著體面的壞論證。每一個經典謬誤，都借用了某個常常合理的樣式的外表；所以比起背名字，更要緊的是看出它在模仿什麼。

paras.en: An argument that is obviously bad does little harm, because nobody is taken in by it. The dangerous ones are those that pass for good. Aristotle opened the first book ever written on the subject with exactly this observation: “That some reasonings are genuine, while others seem to be so but are not, is evident.” It happens, he added, through a certain likeness between the genuine and the sham, in the way that some people are healthy and others only made up to look it. An argument of the second kind is called a fallacy. The word does not mean a false belief, though it is often used that way. It names a fault in the route, and the destination may be true or false.
paras.zh: 一看就知道很糟的論證沒有多大害處，因為沒有人會上當。危險的是那些冒充得了好論證的。亞里斯多德為這個題目寫了史上第一本書，開頭說的正是這件事：「有些推理是真的，另一些看似真的、其實不是，這是很明顯的。」他接著說，這是由於真貨與贗品之間有某種相似，就像有些人是真的健康，有些人只是打扮得像。第二種論證就叫作謬誤。這個詞常被用來指「錯誤的信念」，但那不是它的意思。它說的是路線上的毛病；目的地可以是真的，也可以是假的。

paras.en: The last lesson dealt with formal fallacies, such as affirming the consequent, where the fault lies in the pattern and can be seen with letters in place of words. Most of the fallacies met in daily life are informal. Their form may be unobjectionable. The trouble lies in what the premises say: they are beside the point, or they quietly assume too much, or a word changes its meaning halfway through. Those three troubles give the traditional three families.
paras.zh: 上一課談的是形式謬誤，例如肯定後件：毛病出在樣式上，把詞換成字母也看得出來。日常生活裡遇到的謬誤大多是非形式的。它們的形式可能無可挑剔；問題出在前提說了什麼：前提不相干，或者悄悄預設了太多，或者某個詞在半路換了意思。這三種問題，就是傳統上的三個家族。

paras.en: Fallacies of relevance offer something that moves us in place of something that bears on the question at issue. The ad hominem reply attacks the speaker and leaves the argument standing. One common version, tu quoque (“you too”), tries to discredit advice by pointing out that the adviser does not follow it, as though a doctor who smokes must be wrong about smoking. The appeal to popularity treats the number of believers as evidence. The appeal to authority cites someone eminent on a matter outside his competence: an actor on medicine, a physicist on diet. Appeals to pity or fear work the same way. In every case the premise may well be true, and the conclusion is no more likely for it.
paras.zh: 不相干的謬誤，是拿一個能打動我們的東西，頂替跟爭論中的問題真正有關的東西。人身攻擊（ad hominem）打的是說話的人，論證本身原封不動。常見的一種叫 tu quoque（「你也一樣」）：指出勸告的人自己沒做到，想藉此讓勸告失去效力，好像抽菸的醫生對抽菸的看法就一定是錯的。訴諸群眾，是把相信的人數當成證據。訴諸權威，是引用某位名人對他專長以外的事的看法：演員談醫藥，物理學家談飲食。訴諸憐憫或恐懼也是同一回事。在每一種情形裡，前提很可能是真的，結論卻沒有因此變得更可能為真。

paras.en: Fallacies of presumption smuggle in what they ought to establish. Begging the question assumes the conclusion in the premises, usually in different words. A false dilemma offers two options as though there were no others. A slippery slope asserts, without evidence for each step, that one small move will end in disaster. A hasty generalization leaps from a few cases to all of them. Post hoc ergo propter hoc, “after this, therefore because of this,” infers a cause from a mere sequence. And the straw man misrepresents an opponent’s view in a weaker form, knocks that down, and claims the victory over the original.
paras.zh: 預設型的謬誤，把本該證明的東西偷偷夾帶進來。乞題是在前提裡預設了結論，通常換了一種說法。假兩難只給兩個選項，好像沒有別的可能。滑坡謬誤斷言一小步終將導致災難，卻沒有為中間每一步提出證據。以偏概全從少數個案一躍而到全體。Post hoc ergo propter hoc，「在此之後，所以因此之故」，單憑先後順序就推出因果。稻草人則是把對手的觀點歪曲成比較弱的版本，把那個版本打倒，然後宣稱打敗了原本的觀點。

paras.en: Fallacies of ambiguity turn on language. In equivocation a word is used in two senses, and the argument is valid only if the sense stays fixed. “Nothing is better than good health; a cold sandwich is better than nothing; so a cold sandwich is better than good health.” The joke is harmless, but the same mechanism does real damage when the shifting word is “natural,” “theory,” or “freedom.”
paras.zh: 歧義型的謬誤，關鍵在語言。偷換概念（equivocation）是一個詞用了兩種意思，而論證只有在意思固定不變的時候才有效。「沒有東西比健康更好；冷三明治比沒有東西好；所以冷三明治比健康更好。」這個笑話無傷大雅；可是當那個移動的詞是「自然」「理論」或「自由」的時候，同一套機制就會造成真正的傷害。

paras.en: The most famous case in Chinese philosophy belongs here. Gongsun Long argued in the third century BCE that “a white horse is not a horse” (白馬非馬). The claim is absurd if 非 means “is not a kind of” and quite true if it means “is not identical with,” since the phrase “white horse” picks out color as well as shape. Whether Gongsun Long was committing an equivocation or exposing one is still debated, and that is some measure of how hard ambiguity is to pin down.
paras.zh: 中國哲學裡最有名的例子就屬於這一類。西元前三世紀，公孫龍主張「白馬非馬」。如果「非」的意思是「不屬於」，這個主張很荒謬；如果意思是「不等同於」，它倒是真的，因為「白馬」這個詞除了形，還指定了色。公孫龍究竟是犯了偷換概念，還是在揭發偷換概念，至今仍有爭論；由此多少可以看出，歧義有多難釘住。

paras.en: Here the subject becomes interesting, because almost every item on the list has a respectable twin. Trusting an authority is how any of us knows that the earth is four and a half billion years old; the appeal is fallacious only when the authority is speaking outside his field, or when the experts themselves disagree. A witness’s record of lying is a fact about the person, and it is plainly relevant to whether we should accept his testimony. Some slopes really are slippery, and saying so is reasonable when each step is supported. Even a small sample can justify a conclusion if the cases are known to be alike.
paras.zh: 這門學問到這裡才有意思，因為清單上幾乎每一項都有一個體面的雙胞胎。我們每個人之所以知道地球有四十五億年的歷史，靠的就是信任權威；只有當那位權威談的是專長以外的事，或專家之間自己意見分歧的時候，訴諸權威才是謬誤。證人的說謊紀錄是關於這個人的事實，而它顯然跟我們該不該採信他的證詞有關。有些坡確實是滑的；如果每一步都有根據，指出這一點是合理的。只要已知個案彼此相似，小樣本也可以支持結論。

paras.en: So a fallacy cannot be identified by its outward shape. One has to ask what work the premise is supposed to do and whether it does it. It follows that there is a fallacy about fallacies: to show that an argument is bad is not to show that its conclusion is false. A true claim can be defended badly, and often is.
paras.zh: 所以謬誤沒辦法靠外形辨認。你必須問：這個前提本來應該起什麼作用，它起了沒有？由此還可以推出一個「關於謬誤的謬誤」：證明一個論證不好，並不等於證明它的結論是假的。真的主張可以被辯護得很糟，而且常常如此。

essay.h_zh: 它們為什麼對我們有效

paras.en: If fallacies are so well cataloged, why do they still succeed? Francis Bacon gave the classic answer in 1620. “The human understanding, when any proposition has been once laid down,” he wrote, “forces everything else to add fresh support and confirmation,” and it neglects or explains away the instances on the other side. Psychologists now call this confirmation bias. Fallacies succeed for the most part on the strength of what we already want to believe. That explains the least comfortable fact about them: they are easy to spot in an opponent and almost invisible in a friend.
paras.zh: 既然謬誤早就被整理得這麼清楚，為什麼還是屢屢得逞？培根在 1620 年給了經典的回答。他寫道：「人的理解力，一旦某個命題被確立，就迫使其他一切都來為它增添新的支持與印證」，而對另一邊的事例，則是忽略或設法解釋掉。心理學家現在把這叫作確認偏誤。謬誤多半是憑著我們本來就想相信的東西而得逞的。這也解釋了關於謬誤最令人不舒服的一個事實：在對手身上一眼就看得出來，在朋友身上幾乎看不見。

paras.en: The Latin labels are useful, and they are also a temptation. To answer an argument by shouting “straw man” or “ad hominem” is to stand a label in for a reply, which is itself a failure of relevance. The better practice is slower. Say what the premise was meant to show, say why it does not show it, and then ask whether the argument can be repaired. Often it can. A slippery slope becomes a decent argument once the steps are supported. A hasty generalization becomes a hypothesis worth testing. Used this way, the catalog is less a list of crimes than a set of diagnoses, and its first patient should be oneself.
paras.zh: 這些拉丁文標籤很有用，同時也是一種誘惑。用大喊「稻草人」或「人身攻擊」來回應一個論證，是拿標籤頂替答覆，而這本身就是不相干的毛病。比較好的做法比較慢：說出那個前提原本要證明什麼，說出它為什麼沒有證明到，然後問這個論證修不修得好。常常是修得好的。把每一步都補上根據，滑坡謬誤就成了像樣的論證；以偏概全，可以變成一個值得檢驗的假設。這樣用，這份清單就不像罪名表，而像一組診斷；而它的第一個病人，應該是自己。

lab.lead_en: Eight remarks of the kind you meet every day. For each, choose the diagnosis that fits best. The explanation then shows which respectable pattern the fallacy is imitating, and what it would take to repair the argument.
lab.lead_zh: 八段你每天都會遇到的話。每一段選出最貼切的診斷。解說會告訴你，這個謬誤在模仿哪一個正當的樣式，以及要補上什麼，論證才修得好。

items.src: A comment under a news story · 新聞底下的留言

t.en: “You tell us to eat less meat for the sake of the climate. I saw you eating a beef noodle soup last week.”
t.zh: 「你叫我們為了氣候少吃肉。上禮拜我明明看到你在吃牛肉麵。」

why.en: The speaker’s lunch tells us about the speaker. It tells us nothing about whether eating less meat would help the climate.
why.zh: 說話者吃了什麼，告訴我們的是說話者這個人。至於少吃肉對氣候有沒有幫助，它什麼也沒說。

fix.en: It imitates a fair challenge to a witness. It would be relevant if the question were whether this person is sincere, or whether the advice is practical to follow.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是對證人的正當質疑。如果問題是「這個人是否真誠」或「這個建議做不做得到」，它就是相干的。

items.src: A school board meeting · 學校的會議上

t.en: “Either we ban phones from the school completely, or we accept that our students will learn nothing.”
t.zh: 「我們要嘛全面禁止手機進校園，要嘛就接受學生什麼都學不到。」

why.en: Two extremes are offered as the only choices. Phones kept in lockers, allowed for set tasks, or handed in for certain lessons are all left out.
why.zh: 只給了兩個極端當選項。手機放置物櫃、指定任務時才能用、某些課交出來，這些全被略過了。

fix.en: It imitates a valid pattern: either P or Q; not Q; so P. That pattern is sound only when the two options really are the only ones.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是一個有效樣式：P 或 Q；非 Q；所以 P。只有當這兩個選項真的是僅有的選項時，這個樣式才健全。

items.src: A campaign speech · 競選演說

t.en: “My opponent wants to cut the defense budget by five percent. Apparently he thinks the country does not need to be defended.”
t.zh: 「我的對手想把國防預算砍百分之五。看來他認為這個國家不需要防衛。」

why.en: A modest proposal has been replaced by an absurd one, and the absurd one is then attacked.
why.zh: 一個溫和的提案被換成了荒謬的提案，然後攻擊那個荒謬的。

fix.en: It imitates a reductio, which shows that a view has unacceptable consequences. A real reductio must start from what the opponent actually holds.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是歸謬法：證明一個觀點會導出無法接受的後果。真正的歸謬法，必須從對手實際的主張出發。

items.src: A staff room · 教師辦公室

t.en: “If we let one student retake the exam, soon everyone will demand a retake of everything, and then grades will mean nothing at all.”
t.zh: 「如果我們讓一個學生補考，很快每個人每一科都會要求補考，到時候成績就毫無意義了。」

why.en: Three steps are asserted and none is supported. Each might be stopped by an ordinary rule about who may retake what.
why.zh: 斷言了三步，沒有一步有根據。每一步都可能被一條普通的規定擋下來，例如誰可以補考什麼。

fix.en: It imitates a causal chain. Give evidence for each link, for instance what happened at schools that allowed retakes, and it becomes a real argument.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是因果鏈。替每一環提出證據，例如允許補考的學校後來怎麼了，它就成了真正的論證。

items.src: A sports fan · 一位球迷

t.en: “I wore my red socks to the last three games and we won all three. I am wearing them to the final.”
t.zh: 「前三場比賽我都穿紅襪子，三場都贏了。決賽我也要穿。」

why.en: The wins came after the socks. Nothing shows that they came because of them.
why.zh: 贏球發生在穿襪子之後。沒有任何東西顯示，贏球是因為襪子。

fix.en: It imitates causal inference, which also begins from a sequence. What is missing is a comparison: the games played without the socks, and some idea of how socks could matter.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是因果推論，因果推論也是從先後順序出發的。它缺的是對照：沒穿那雙襪子的比賽結果如何，以及襪子究竟可能怎麼起作用。

t.en: “Our newspaper is the most trustworthy in the country. You can be sure of that, because we print only what is reliable.”
t.zh: 「本報是全國最值得信賴的報紙。這一點您可以放心，因為我們只刊登可靠的內容。」

why.en: The reason given for trusting the paper is the paper’s own claim to be trustworthy. The conclusion has been used as its own premise.
why.zh: 信任這份報紙的理由，是這份報紙自稱值得信賴。結論被拿來當成它自己的前提。

fix.en: It imitates a valid argument, and in fact it is one: P, therefore P. The repair is an independent reason, such as a record of corrections or an outside audit.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是有效論證，而且它確實有效：P，所以 P。要修好它，得有一個獨立的理由，例如更正紀錄或外部稽核。

items.src: A product page · 產品頁面

t.en: “This supplement ends tiredness for good. A well-known film actor takes it every morning and recommends it.”
t.zh: 「這款保健食品徹底消除疲勞。一位知名電影演員每天早上都吃，而且推薦它。」

why.en: Fame is not expertise. The actor’s opinion on physiology carries no more weight than anyone else’s.
why.zh: 名氣不是專業。這位演員對生理學的看法，並不比任何人更有分量。

fix.en: It imitates a legitimate appeal to expert testimony. Replace the actor with controlled trials, or with the agreed view of specialists, and the form is fine.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是正當的專家證言。把演員換成對照試驗，或換成專科醫師的共識，這個形式就沒有問題。

items.src: A classroom debate · 課堂辯論

t.en: “Evolution is only a theory. A theory is just a guess. So evolution is just a guess.”
t.zh: 「演化只是一個理論。理論不過是猜測。所以演化不過是猜測。」

why.en: “Theory” means a well-tested explanatory system in the first premise and a hunch in the second. With one meaning held fixed, one of the premises is false.
why.zh: 「理論」在第一個前提裡指的是經過充分檢驗的解釋體系，在第二個前提裡指的是臆測。把意思固定成一種，就有一個前提是假的。

fix.en: It imitates a valid syllogism. A syllogism needs exactly three terms, and this one has four, two of them spelled alike.
fix.zh: 它模仿的是有效的三段論。三段論恰好需要三個詞項，這個論證有四個，其中兩個拼法相同。

items: Rejecting a claim because of who makes it.
Rejecting advice because the adviser does not follow it.
Citing someone eminent outside his field.
Treating the number of believers as evidence.
Offering pity or fear in place of a reason.
Assuming the conclusion in the premises.
Presenting two options as the only ones.
Concluding about all from too few.
Inferring a cause from a sequence.
Attacking a weakened version of a view.
Using one word in two senses.
Trading on a sentence that can be parsed two ways.

argument.lead_en: Why is an attack on the speaker supposed to be irrelevant? The standard case against ad hominem can be set out as an argument, and it has a weak point worth finding. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 為什麼攻擊說話的人被認為是不相干的？反對人身攻擊的標準理由可以攤開成一個論證，而它有一個值得找出來的弱點。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Whether a claim is true depends on how things are, and not on who asserts it.
steps.zh: 一個主張是不是真的，取決於事情實際如何，不取決於是誰說的。
steps.ob_en: Rarely attacked. The exceptions are claims about the speaker (“I am in pain”) and promises, where who is speaking is part of what is said.
steps.ob_zh: 很少被攻擊。例外是關於說話者本人的主張（「我很痛」）以及承諾；在這些情況下，誰在說話本身就是內容的一部分。

steps.en: An ad hominem reply offers a fact about the speaker as a reason to reject the claim.
steps.zh: 人身攻擊式的回應，是拿關於說話者的一項事實，當作拒絕該主張的理由。
steps.ob_en: This is a definition and is not in dispute.

steps.en: Facts about the speaker are no evidence about how things are.
steps.zh: 關於說話者的事實，不構成事情實際如何的證據。
steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked. When our only reason for believing a claim is that someone says so, the speaker’s reliability is exactly the evidence we have. A paid witness, a record of lying, or a conflict of interest lowers the weight of testimony, and courts treat such facts as relevant every day.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步。當我們相信某個主張的唯一理由是「有人這麼說」，說話者可不可靠，恰恰就是我們手上的證據。收了錢的證人、說謊的紀錄、利益衝突，都會降低證詞的分量；法庭每天都把這類事實當作相干的。

steps.en: Therefore an ad hominem reply gives no reason to reject the claim.
steps.zh: 所以，人身攻擊式的回應，並沒有提供拒絕該主張的理由。
steps.ob_en: The conclusion holds when the speaker has given an argument, for then the argument can be judged on its merits and the speaker drops out. It fails when the speaker has given only his word. The fallacy lies in treating the first situation as if it were the second.
steps.ob_zh: 當說話者提出了論證，結論成立：這時論證可以就它本身來評判，說話者可以擱在一邊。當說話者只給了他的「話」，結論就不成立。謬誤在於把第一種情況當成第二種來處理。

source.work: Aristotle, Sophistical Refutations; John Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding
source.work_zh: 亞里斯多德《辯謬篇》；洛克《人類理解論》
source.tr: Aristotle translated by W. A. Pickard-Cambridge; Locke in the original English (both public domain)
source.lead_en: The study of fallacies begins with Aristotle’s short treatise on the tricks of professional debaters. Two thousand years later John Locke gave several fallacies the Latin names they still carry.
source.lead_zh: 對謬誤的研究，始於亞里斯多德談職業辯士伎倆的一篇短論。兩千年後，洛克替其中幾種謬誤取了沿用至今的拉丁文名字。

passages.en: That some reasonings are genuine, while others seem to be so but are not, is evident. This happens with arguments, as also elsewhere, through a certain likeness between the genuine and the sham.
passages.zh: 有些推理是真的，另一些看似真的、其實不是，這是很明顯的。在論證上會如此，就像在別的地方一樣，是由於真貨與贗品之間有某種相似。
passages.note_en: The whole theory is in the word “likeness.” A fallacy is defined by reference to the good argument it resembles, which is why every item in the exercise above has an “it imitates” line. Aristotle went on to list thirteen types, six that depend on language and seven that do not, and most modern lists descend from his.
passages.note_zh: 整套理論都在「相似」這個詞裡。謬誤是參照它所模仿的好論證來界定的；所以上面練習裡的每一題，都有一行「它模仿的是」。亞里斯多德接著列出十三種：六種依賴語言，七種不依賴；現代的清單大多是從他那裡傳下來的。

passages.en: The first is, to allege the opinions of men, whose parts, learning, eminency, power, or some other cause has gained a name, and settled their reputation in the common esteem with some kind of authority.
passages.zh: 第一種，是援引某些人的意見；這些人的才能、學問、顯赫、權勢或別的原因，使他們博得了名聲，並且在公眾的評價裡確立了某種權威。
passages.note_en: Locke calls this argumentum ad verecundiam, the argument addressed to modesty, because the hearer is made to feel that doubting such a person would be insolent. Notice where he locates the fault. He does not say authorities are usually wrong. He says the argument works by shaming the listener into silence and so produces assent without knowledge. (“Parts” here means abilities.)
passages.note_zh: 洛克把這稱為 argumentum ad verecundiam，「訴諸謙遜的論證」，因為它讓聽的人覺得，懷疑這樣的人物就是無禮。注意他把毛病放在哪裡。他沒有說權威通常是錯的。他說的是：這種論證靠著讓聽者羞於開口而奏效，所以產生的是沒有知識的同意。（這裡的 parts 是「才能」的意思。）

items.o_en: The list of fallacies is a ragbag. It has no principle behind it, textbooks disagree about what belongs on it, and learning thirty Latin names teaches nobody to reason.
items.o_zh: 謬誤清單是個大雜燴。它背後沒有原則，各家教科書對該收哪些意見不一；背三十個拉丁文名字，教不會任何人推理。
items.r_en: The charge was made forcefully by the logician C. L. Hamblin in 1970, and much of it sticks: the traditional list grew by accident. But a field guide can be useful without being a theory. What matters is that each entry be taught together with its legitimate twin, so that the student learns a question to ask instead of a label to apply.
items.r_zh: 邏輯學家漢布林在 1970 年有力地提出過這項指控，而且大半說中了：傳統清單是偶然累積起來的。不過，野外圖鑑不必是理論，也可以有用。要緊的是，每一項都要連同它正當的雙胞胎一起教，讓學生學到的是一個該問的問題，而不是一個可以貼的標籤。

items.o_en: Many so-called fallacies are sensible shortcuts. Nobody can check everything personally, so going along with experts and with the majority is what a rational person with limited time ought to do.
items.o_zh: 許多所謂的謬誤，其實是明智的捷徑。沒有人能事事親自查證；所以跟著專家、跟著多數人走，正是時間有限的理性人應該做的。
items.r_en: This is right, and it corrects a common misuse of the subject. Such appeals fail as proofs and succeed, often, as evidence. The mistake is to treat a defeasible reason, one that holds only until something overrides it, as if it settled the matter. On this view, to call something a fallacy is to say that its support has been overstated.
items.r_zh: 這是對的，而且糾正了這門學問常見的誤用。這類訴求當作證明是失敗的，當作證據卻常常是成功的。錯誤在於把一個「可被推翻的理由」——在沒有別的東西壓過它之前才成立的理由——當成一錘定音。照這個看法，說某個東西是謬誤，意思是說：它提供的支持被誇大了。

items.o_en: Fallacy-spotting makes people worse. It hands them a vocabulary for dismissing whatever they dislike.
items.o_zh: 抓謬誤會讓人變得更糟。它給了人一套詞彙，用來打發一切他不喜歡的東西。
items.r_en: There is evidence for the worry, since more skilled reasoners are often better at defending what they already believe. The remedy is the order of application. Use the catalog on your own side first, state the other side’s argument in its strongest form before criticizing it, and remember that a refuted argument leaves its conclusion standing.
items.r_zh: 這個擔憂是有根據的：比較會推理的人，常常只是更擅長替自己原本的信念辯護。解方在於使用的順序。先把這份清單用在自己這一邊；批評之前，先把對方的論證用最強的形式說出來；並且記得，論證被駁倒了，它的結論仍然站著。

said.claim: “Ad hominem” has always meant attacking the person.
said.claim_zh: 「Ad hominem」向來就是攻擊個人的意思。
said.en: When Locke described the argumentum ad hominem in 1690, he meant something else: “to press a man with consequences drawn from his own principles or concessions.” That is, to argue from premises the other person has already accepted, which is a fair move and is what Socrates did all day. The sense of personal abuse became standard only later.
said.zh: 洛克在 1690 年描述 argumentum ad hominem 的時候，指的是另一回事：「用從一個人自己的原則或讓步引出來的後果去逼他。」也就是從對方已經接受的前提出發來論證；這是正當的一招，蘇格拉底整天做的就是這個。「人身辱罵」的意思是後來才成為通行用法的。

terms.d_en: An argument that seems better than it is. Not a synonym for “false belief.”
terms.d_zh: 看起來比實際上好的論證。不是「錯誤信念」的同義詞。

terms.d_en: Rejecting a claim on the ground of facts about the person who makes it.
terms.d_zh: 以關於說話者的事實為由，拒絕他的主張。

terms.d_en: Dismissing a criticism because the critic is guilty of the same thing.
terms.d_zh: 因為批評者自己也犯同樣的毛病，就不理會他的批評。

terms.d_en: A distorted, weaker version of an opponent’s position, set up to be knocked down.
terms.d_zh: 把對手的立場扭曲成比較弱的版本，立起來好打倒。

terms.d_en: Presenting two alternatives as though they were the only ones.
terms.d_zh: 把兩個選項說成僅有的選項。

terms.d_en: Using a word in two senses within one argument.
terms.d_zh: 在同一個論證裡，一個詞用了兩種意思。

terms.o: L. ‘after this, therefore because of this’
terms.d_en: Inferring that one event caused another merely because it came first.
terms.d_zh: 只因為一件事先發生，就推斷它造成了後一件事。

terms.o: L. via Old French desfaire ‘to undo’
terms.d_en: Said of a reason that supports a conclusion unless further information overrides it.
terms.d_zh: 形容這樣的理由：它支持結論，除非有進一步的資訊壓過它。

terms.d_en: The tendency to notice and favor evidence for what one already believes.
terms.d_zh: 傾向於注意並偏好支持自己既有信念的證據。

vocab.eg: Nobody is taken in by an argument that is obviously bad.
vocab.eg_zh: 一看就很糟的論證，沒有人會上當。

vocab.eg: The dangerous arguments are those that pass for good.
vocab.eg_zh: 危險的論證，是那些冒充得了好論證的。

vocab.eg: The premise does not bear on the question at issue.
vocab.eg_zh: 這個前提跟爭論中的問題無關。

vocab.eg: Tu quoque tries to discredit advice by attacking the adviser.
vocab.eg_zh: 「你也一樣」想藉著攻擊勸告者，讓勸告失去效力。

vocab.eg: Fallacies of presumption smuggle in what they ought to establish.
vocab.eg_zh: 預設型的謬誤，把本該證明的東西偷偷夾帶進來。

vocab.eg: The straw man misrepresents an opponent’s view in a weaker form.
vocab.eg_zh: 稻草人把對手的觀點歪曲成比較弱的版本。

vocab.eg: Fallacies of ambiguity turn on language.
vocab.eg_zh: 歧義型的謬誤，關鍵在語言。

vocab.eg: Ambiguity is hard to pin down.
vocab.eg_zh: 歧義很難釘住。

vocab.eg: It neglects or explains away the instances on the other side.
vocab.eg_zh: 對另一邊的事例，它忽略或設法解釋掉。

vocab.eg: Fallacies succeed on the strength of what we already want to believe.
vocab.eg_zh: 謬誤是憑著我們本來就想相信的東西而得逞的。

quiz.q: How does the essay define a fallacy?
options: An argument that seems better than it is.
Any false statement.
An argument with a false conclusion.
An argument that most people reject.

quiz.q: When is an appeal to authority reasonable, according to the essay?
options: When the authority is speaking within his field and the experts broadly agree.
Whenever the authority is famous.
Never.
Only when the authority has been dead for a long time.

quiz.q: What is the “fallacy about fallacies”?
options: Concluding that a claim is false because an argument for it is bad.
Using Latin names for fallacies.
Believing that fallacies do not exist.
Committing two fallacies in one argument.

quiz.q: Why, on Bacon’s account, do fallacies keep succeeding?
options: We look for support for what we already believe and neglect what counts against it.
Most people have never studied Latin.
Fallacies are usually valid.
Opponents hide their premises.

quiz.q: What did Locke originally mean by argumentum ad hominem?
options: Pressing a person with consequences drawn from his own principles.
Insulting a person’s character.
Citing a famous person’s opinion.
Arguing from the opinion of the majority.

write.en: Collect three fallacies from this week’s news, advertising, or social media. For each, name it, say which legitimate pattern it imitates, and rewrite it as a better argument for the same conclusion.
write.zh: 從這禮拜的新聞、廣告或社群媒體蒐集三個謬誤。每一個都說出名稱、說明它模仿哪一個正當的樣式，再把它改寫成支持同一個結論的更好論證。

write.en: Describe a belief of your own that you once defended with a bad argument. What was the fallacy, and do you still hold the belief?
write.zh: 描述一個你自己的信念，你曾經用一個壞論證替它辯護。那是哪一種謬誤？你現在還持有這個信念嗎？

write.en: Is it ever reasonable to believe something because most people believe it? Answer in about 150 words, with one example on each side.
write.zh: 「因為大多數人相信，所以我也相信」，這有合理的時候嗎？用大約 150 個英文字回答，正反各舉一個例子。

paras.en: The discourse to the Kālāmas (Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.65) reads in places like a list of fallacies of relevance. The Buddha tells a puzzled town not to settle a question by oral tradition, by lineage, by hearsay, by the authority of scripture, by the speaker’s apparent competence, or by the thought “this ascetic is our teacher.” The list also includes “by logic” and “by inference,” which shows that it is not a charter for free thinking, as it is often taken to be. Its point is that none of these sources is sufficient by itself. The test he gives is practical: whether a thing, when taken up, leads to harm or to welfare.
paras.zh: 對伽藍族人所說的那部經（《增支部》3.65），有些段落讀起來像一份不相干謬誤的清單。佛陀告訴一個感到困惑的城鎮：不要因為口耳相傳、因為傳承、因為傳聞、因為合於經典的權威、因為說者看似有能力，或者因為「這位沙門是我們的老師」，就據以論定一個問題。這份清單也包括「因為邏輯」與「因為推論」；可見它並不像一般常說的那樣，是一份自由思想的宣言。它的重點是：這些來源沒有一個單憑自己就足夠。他給的檢驗是實踐上的：一件事，照著去做，是導向損害，還是導向利益。

paras.en: Buddhist logicians later did something the Western tradition did not manage. They derived their fallacies from a single principle. Dignāga held that a good reason must satisfy three conditions (trairūpya): it must be a property of the subject, it must be present in similar cases, and it must be absent from all dissimilar cases. A fallacious reason (hetvābhāsa, 似因) is one that fails a condition, and so there are three kinds: the unestablished, the inconclusive, and the contradictory. Hamblin’s complaint that the Western list has no principle behind it does not apply here. The price is narrowness: the scheme covers faults of inference and has nothing to say about a straw man (Dharma and the West, D14).
paras.zh: 佛教的邏輯學家後來做到了一件西方傳統沒做成的事：從單一原則推導出他們的謬誤。陳那主張，好的「因」必須滿足三個條件（因三相，trairūpya）：它必須是主題所具有的性質（遍是宗法性），必須在同類事例中出現（同品定有性），必須在一切異類事例中都不出現（異品遍無性）。似因（hetvābhāsa）就是不滿足其中某個條件的因，所以有三類：不成、不定、相違。漢布林抱怨西方的清單背後沒有原則，這個抱怨在這裡用不上。代價是範圍窄：這套架構涵蓋的是推論上的過失，對稻草人這類毛病無話可說（佛法與西方哲學 D14）。

terms: the three marks of a good reason
