lessons.title: Can You Ever Catch the Tortoise?
lessons.blurb_en: Paradoxes: arguments that start from what everyone accepts, proceed by steps no one can fault, and arrive at what no one can believe.
lessons.blurb_zh: 悖論：從人人接受的前提出發，每一步都挑不出毛病，卻走到沒有人能相信的結論。
lessons.big_en: A paradox shows that some belief we hold must be wrong without telling us which. That is why paradoxes, more than any other kind of argument, have forced people to rebuild their basic concepts.
lessons.big_zh: 悖論告訴我們，我們的某個信念一定錯了，卻不告訴我們是哪一個。所以悖論比任何別種論證，都更能逼人重建自己的基本概念。

paras.en: The last two lessons were about telling good arguments from bad ones. A paradox is the case where that skill gives out. The premises look true. Each step looks valid. And the conclusion is something no sane person accepts: that the fastest runner cannot catch the slowest, that a sentence is true and false at once, that there is no such thing as a heap of sand. Since a sound argument cannot have a false conclusion, something must give way, and there are only three choices. One of the premises is false after all. Or one of the steps is invalid. Or the conclusion, incredible as it seems, is true. Philosophers call the third option biting the bullet, and the history of the subject is full of people who did.
paras.zh: 前兩課談的是分辨好論證與壞論證。悖論，是這項本事失靈的地方。前提看起來是真的；每一步看起來都有效；而結論是任何神智正常的人都不接受的：跑得最快的人追不上最慢的；一個句子同時又真又假；世界上沒有「一堆沙」這種東西。既然健全的論證不可能有假的結論，總得有什麼東西讓步，而選擇只有三個：原來有一個前提是假的；或者有一步是無效的；或者那個結論，儘管看來難以置信，卻是真的。哲學家把第三種選擇叫作「咬子彈」（硬著頭皮接受），而這門學問的歷史上，這樣做的人多得是。

paras.en: The oldest paradoxes we have come from Zeno of Elea, a Greek of the fifth century BCE. His teacher Parmenides had argued that reality is one and unchanging and that motion is an appearance. Zeno defended him by showing that the commonsense view, on which things move, leads to absurdities of its own. Aristotle preserves the most famous of his arguments: “in a race the quickest runner can never overtake the slowest, since the pursuer must first reach the point whence the pursued started, so that the slower must always hold a lead.”
paras.zh: 我們手上最古老的悖論出自埃利亞的芝諾，西元前五世紀的希臘人。他的老師巴門尼德主張，實在是唯一而不變的，運動只是表象。芝諾替老師辯護的方式，是證明常識的看法——東西會動——自己會導出荒謬。亞里斯多德保存了他最有名的一個論證：「在賽跑中，跑得最快的永遠追不上最慢的，因為追的人必須先到達被追的人出發的那一點，所以慢的那個必定一直保持領先。」

paras.en: Give the slow runner a start of a hundred meters. By the time Achilles has covered the hundred, the other has crept forward ten. By the time Achilles has covered those ten, it is one meter further on, and so without end. At every stage a gap remains. The stages never run out. So it seems that Achilles is always on the point of drawing level and never does.
paras.zh: 讓慢的那個先跑一百公尺。等阿基里斯跑完這一百公尺，對方已經往前爬了十公尺。等阿基里斯跑完這十公尺，牠又在前面一公尺了；如此下去，沒有盡頭。每一個階段都還剩一段差距，而階段永遠用不完。於是看起來，阿基里斯永遠就要追平，卻永遠沒有追平。

paras.en: Chinese thinkers found the same puzzle independently. The last chapter of the Zhuangzi records a saying of the debaters around Hui Shi, in the fourth century BCE: “A stick one foot long: take away half of it every day, and in ten thousand generations it will not be used up.” This is Zeno’s other great argument, the Dichotomy, turned from motion to matter. Before you reach the door you must reach the halfway point, and before that the halfway point of the first half. Run in one direction the argument says you never arrive, and run in the other it says you can never set out.
paras.zh: 中國的思想家各自獨立地發現了同一個難題。《莊子》最後一篇記下了西元前四世紀惠施周圍那群辯者的一句話：「一尺之捶，日取其半，萬世不竭。」這是芝諾另一個重要論證「二分法」，只是從運動換成了物質。你走到門口之前，必須先走到一半；在那之前，又必須先走到前一半的一半。這個論證往一個方向推，說你永遠到不了；往另一個方向推，說你根本出發不了。

essay.h_en: The sum of infinitely many things

paras.en: The standard answer took two thousand years to state properly. Zeno assumes that infinitely many distances, or infinitely many intervals of time, must add up to an infinite amount. They need not. The distances in the race are 100, 10, 1, 0.1 and so on, and the more of them you add, the closer the total comes to 111.11… meters without ever exceeding it. Mathematicians of the nineteenth century, Cauchy foremost among them, made this exact with the concept of a limit. The times behave the same way. If Achilles runs ten meters a second, the stages take 10 seconds, then 1, then 0.1, and all of them together take 11.11… seconds. After that he is in front.
paras.zh: 標準答案花了兩千年才被說清楚。芝諾假定，無窮多段距離，或無窮多段時間，加起來一定是無窮大。其實不必。賽跑裡的各段距離是 100、10、1、0.1……，你加進去的項愈多，總和就愈接近 111.11… 公尺，卻永遠不會超過它。十九世紀的數學家，以柯西為首，用「極限」這個概念把這件事說得精確。時間也是同樣的情形。如果阿基里斯每秒跑十公尺，各階段分別花 10 秒、1 秒、0.1 秒……，全部加起來是 11.11… 秒。在那之後，他就在前面了。

paras.en: Many philosophers think this dissolves the paradox, and many do not. The arithmetic tells us where and when Achilles draws level. It does not obviously tell us how anyone finishes a sequence of tasks that has no last member. In 1954 James Thomson sharpened the worry with a lamp. Switch it on for a minute, off for half a minute, on for a quarter, and so on; after two minutes infinitely many switchings are done. Is the lamp then on or off? It cannot be on, since every time it was turned on it was turned off again, and it cannot be off for the same reason. Thomson concluded that completing infinitely many tasks, a “supertask,” is impossible. His critics replied that the story merely fails to say what happens at two minutes. The argument continues, and what is at stake in it is whether space, time, and motion are really as the mathematics of the continuum describes them.
paras.zh: 許多哲學家認為這樣就化解了悖論，也有許多人不這麼想。算術告訴我們阿基里斯在哪裡、在什麼時候追平。可是，一個沒有「最後一項」的任務序列，到底是怎麼被做完的，算術並沒有明白地告訴我們。1954 年，湯姆森用一盞燈把這個疑慮磨得更尖。把燈打開一分鐘，關掉半分鐘，再開四分之一分鐘，如此下去；兩分鐘後，無窮多次開關都做完了。這時燈是亮的還是暗的？它不可能是亮的，因為每一次打開之後都又被關掉了；基於同樣的理由，它也不可能是暗的。湯姆森的結論是：完成無窮多個任務，也就是所謂的「超任務」，是不可能的。批評他的人回答說，這個故事只是沒有交代兩分鐘那一刻發生了什麼。這場爭論還在繼續；而它真正牽涉到的是：空間、時間與運動，是不是真的像連續統的數學所描述的那樣。

essay.h_en: A sentence that turns on itself
essay.h_zh: 一個回頭咬自己的句子

paras.en: A second family of paradoxes needs no racetrack, only a sentence. Consider: “This sentence is false.” If it is true, then what it says is the case, so it is false. If it is false, then what it says is not the case, so it is true. The ancient version is credited to Eubulides, a contemporary of Aristotle, and it is known as the Liar. It is tempting to dismiss the Liar as a trick, and for two thousand years most people did. Then, in the early twentieth century, the same structure of self-reference turned up in the foundations of mathematics. Bertrand Russell found it in the notion of a set, and Kurt Gödel used a relative of the Liar, a sentence that says of itself that it cannot be proved, to show that arithmetic contains truths no consistent system of rules can derive. Alfred Tarski’s response to the Liar was that no language can contain its own truth predicate: to say of a sentence that it is true, one has to step up into a richer language. Ordinary English falls short of that standard, which may mean that ordinary English is, strictly speaking, inconsistent.
paras.zh: 第二個家族的悖論不需要跑道，只需要一個句子。請看：「這個句子是假的。」如果它是真的，那麼它說的就是事實，所以它是假的。如果它是假的，那麼它說的就不是事實，所以它是真的。它的古代版本相傳出自與亞里斯多德同時代的歐布利德斯，稱為「說謊者悖論」。把說謊者當成文字把戲打發掉，是很誘人的做法；兩千年來，多數人正是這樣做的。然後在二十世紀初，同一種自我指涉的結構，出現在數學的基礎裡。羅素在「集合」這個概念裡發現了它；哥德爾則用了說謊者的一個親戚——一個說自己「不可被證明」的句子——證明算術裡有些真理，是任何一致的規則系統都推導不出來的。塔斯基對說謊者的回應是：沒有任何語言能包含它自己的「真」這個謂詞；要說一個句子是真的，就得往上跨進一個更豐富的語言。日常的英語達不到這個標準；這也許表示，嚴格說來，日常的英語是不一致的。

paras.en: Eubulides is also credited with the paradox of the heap, the sorites. One grain of sand is not a heap. Adding a single grain to something that is not a heap never turns it into one. So no number of grains makes a heap. Each premise seems undeniable, the logic is modus ponens repeated, and the conclusion is false. What makes the sorites so hard is that the trouble is everywhere. “Heap” is vague, and so are “tall,” “adult,” “alive,” and “person,” and the same argument can be run on each of them. Law and ethics depend on such words, and on lines that have to be drawn somewhere although no particular place for them can be defended.
paras.zh: 相傳「堆垛悖論」（sorites）也出自歐布利德斯。一粒沙不是一堆。在不成堆的東西上加一粒沙，絕不會讓它變成一堆。所以不管多少粒沙，都不成一堆。每一個前提看來都無法否認，邏輯只是反覆使用肯定前件，而結論是假的。堆垛悖論之所以這麼難，是因為問題無所不在。「堆」是模糊的，「高」「成年」「活著」「人」也都是；同一個論證可以套在每一個詞上。法律與倫理都仰賴這類詞語，也仰賴那些總得畫在某處的界線；儘管沒有哪一個特定的位置能被辯護。

paras.en: It would be a mistake to file all this under puzzles. A paradox is an argument that our own concepts make against us. It shows that what we believe about motion, or truth, or the meaning of ordinary words cannot all be right together, and it does so using nothing except those beliefs. The great ones are therefore never simply solved. They are answered by changing something: by inventing the limit, or separating a language from its metalanguage, or by rethinking what a set is. With this the first unit ends, on a caution. Logic can show us that our premises conflict. It does not tell us which of them to give up.
paras.zh: 把這一切歸到「益智謎題」那一類，會是個錯誤。悖論是我們自己的概念對我們提出的論證。它證明我們對運動、對真、對日常詞語意義的種種信念，不可能同時全部正確；而且它除了這些信念之外，什麼都沒用到。所以偉大的悖論從來不是單純被「解開」的。回應它們的方式，是改變某樣東西：發明極限，或把一個語言跟它的後設語言分開，或重新思考集合是什麼。第一個單元就在這裡結束，結束在一句提醒上：邏輯能告訴我們，我們的前提互相衝突；它不告訴我們該放棄哪一個。

lab.title_en: Try it: run the race two ways
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：用兩種方式跑這場比賽
lab.lead_en: First run the race Zeno’s way, one stage at a time, and watch the gap shrink without ever closing. Then let the clock run and watch Achilles go past. The same race is being described both times, and the paradox is the question of how both descriptions can be right.
lab.lead_zh: 先照芝諾的方式跑，一次一個階段，看差距不斷縮小卻始終沒有合上。然後讓時鐘自己走，看阿基里斯超過去。兩次描述的是同一場比賽；悖論就是在問：這兩種描述怎麼可能都對？
lab.note_en: Achilles runs 10 meters a second. The tortoise starts 100 meters ahead.
lab.note_zh: 阿基里斯每秒跑 10 公尺。烏龜從前方 100 公尺處出發。

argument.lead_en: Set out step by step, the Achilles has four premises. Anyone who rejects the conclusion owes Zeno an answer to the question of which one is false. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 一步一步攤開來，阿基里斯論證有四個前提。任何不接受結論的人，都欠芝諾一個答案：哪一個前提是假的？點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: To catch the tortoise, Achilles must first reach the point where the tortoise was when he set out.
steps.zh: 要追上烏龜，阿基里斯必須先到達他出發時烏龜所在的那一點。
steps.ob_en: Hardly deniable, given that he runs along the same line. This premise only describes the race.
steps.ob_zh: 既然他沿著同一條線跑，這幾乎無法否認。這個前提只是在描述比賽。

steps.en: Whenever Achilles reaches a point where the tortoise was, the tortoise has moved some distance ahead.
steps.zh: 每當阿基里斯到達烏龜曾經在的某一點，烏龜已經往前移動了一段距離。
steps.ob_en: True for as long as the tortoise is ahead. Some reply that the premise quietly restricts our attention to the period before the catch and so cannot tell us what happens at it.
steps.ob_zh: 只要烏龜還在前面，這就是真的。有人回應說：這個前提悄悄把我們的注意力限制在「追上之前」那段時間，所以它無法告訴我們追上的那一刻發生了什麼。

steps.en: So before he catches it, Achilles must complete infinitely many runs, one after another.
steps.zh: 所以在追上之前，阿基里斯必須一個接一個，完成無窮多段的跑。
steps.ob_en: Aristotle attacked here. The stretches are only potentially infinite, he said: the run is one continuous motion, and it is we who divide it in thought. If space and time were made of smallest units, the division would also come to an end, though Zeno had other arguments against that view.
steps.ob_zh: 亞里斯多德攻擊的是這裡。他說，這些段落只是「潛在地」無窮：跑步是一個連續的運動，是我們在思想裡把它切開的。如果空間與時間由最小單位構成，分割也會有盡頭；不過芝諾另有論證反對那種看法。

steps.en: No one can complete infinitely many runs in a finite time.
steps.zh: 沒有人能在有限的時間內完成無窮多段的跑。
steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked. If each run takes a tenth of the time of the one before, the times form a series with a finite sum, 11.11… seconds. The premise treats “infinitely many” as if it meant “infinitely long.” Whether a finite sum fully explains how an endless sequence gets finished is the point Thomson and others have pressed.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步。如果每一段所花的時間是前一段的十分之一，這些時間構成一個總和有限的級數：11.11… 秒。這個前提把「無窮多」當成了「無窮長」。至於一個有限的總和，是否就完全解釋了一個沒有盡頭的序列怎麼被做完，那正是湯姆森等人追問的地方。

steps.en: Therefore Achilles never catches the tortoise.
steps.zh: 所以阿基里斯永遠追不上烏龜。
steps.ob_en: Zeno accepted the conclusion, or something stronger: that motion itself is not real. Almost everyone since has taken the argument as a reductio of one of its premises. The interest lies in the disagreement about which.
steps.ob_zh: 芝諾接受這個結論，或者說接受一個更強的結論：運動本身不是真實的。此後幾乎所有人都把這個論證看成對它某個前提的歸謬。有意思的地方在於，大家對「是哪一個」意見不一。

source.work_zh: 亞里斯多德《物理學》卷六第九章；《莊子・天下》
source.tr: Aristotle translated by R. P. Hardie and R. K. Gaye (public domain); the Zhuangzi line in our own translation
source.lead_en: Zeno’s book is lost. Everything we know of his arguments comes from later writers, and chiefly from Aristotle, who reports them in order to refute them.
source.lead_zh: 芝諾的書失傳了。我們對他論證的了解全部來自後來的作者，主要是亞里斯多德；而亞里斯多德記下它們，是為了反駁。

passages.en: The second is the so-called ‘Achilles’, and it amounts to this, that in a race the quickest runner can never overtake the slowest, since the pursuer must first reach the point whence the pursued started, so that the slower must always hold a lead.
passages.zh: 第二個是所謂的「阿基里斯」，它的大意是：在賽跑中，跑得最快的永遠追不上最慢的，因為追的人必須先到達被追的人出發的那一點，所以慢的那個必定一直保持領先。
passages.note_en: Three things to notice. “So-called” shows that the argument already had its nickname in Aristotle’s day. There is no tortoise: the text says only “the slowest.” And the whole argument is a single sentence, which means that the four-premise version above is a reconstruction. Reconstructing an argument from a hostile summary is a large part of what historians of philosophy do. (“Whence” means “from which.”)
passages.note_zh: 有三件事值得注意。「所謂的」表示這個論證在亞里斯多德的時代已經有了綽號。裡面沒有烏龜：原文只說「最慢的」。而整個論證只有一句話；也就是說，上面那個四個前提的版本是重建出來的。從一份帶有敵意的摘要重建論證，是哲學史家工作的一大部分。（whence 是「從那裡」的意思。）

passages.en: A stick one foot long: take away half of it every day, and in ten thousand generations it will not be used up.
passages.zh: 一尺之捶，日取其半，萬世不竭。
passages.note_en: The line appears in a list of twenty-one sayings with which the debaters “responded to Hui Shi.” No argument is given for any of them. The Greek paradox comes down to us with its reasoning and without its author’s book, and the Chinese one with a bare conclusion, so that we have to supply the reasoning ourselves. The author of the chapter was not impressed: such men, he says, could defeat people’s mouths and could not win their hearts.
passages.note_zh: 這句話出現在辯者「與惠施相應」的二十一條說法當中，沒有一條附上論證。希臘的悖論傳到我們手上，有推理而沒有作者的書；中國的這一條只有光禿禿的結論，推理得由我們自己補。寫這一篇的人對他們不以為然：他說這些人「能勝人之口，不能服人之心」。

items.o_en: Calculus solved Zeno’s paradoxes long ago. Only philosophers still pretend there is a problem.
items.o_zh: 微積分早就解決了芝諾的悖論。只有哲學家還在假裝這裡有問題。
items.r_en: Calculus shows that the infinite series has a finite sum, and so refutes the premise that infinitely many runs need infinite time. It does not by itself show that physical space and time are infinitely divisible, as the mathematics assumes, and it does not say what it is to complete a sequence with no last step. One may think those further questions have good answers. They are still questions, and they are not answered by doing the sum.
items.r_zh: 微積分證明了這個無窮級數有有限的總和，因此駁倒了「無窮多段的跑需要無窮長的時間」這個前提。但它本身並沒有證明物理的空間與時間像數學所假定的那樣可以無限分割，也沒有說明「做完一個沒有最後一步的序列」是怎麼一回事。你可以認為這些進一步的問題都有好答案。它們仍然是問題，而且不是算出總和就回答了的。

items.o_en: The Liar is not a real sentence. A sentence that talks about itself says nothing, so it is neither true nor false and there is no paradox.
items.o_zh: 說謊者根本不是真正的句子。一個談論自己的句子什麼也沒說，所以它既不真也不假，沒有悖論可言。
items.r_en: Self-reference as such is harmless: “This sentence has five words” is plainly true. And the proposed way out leads straight back in. Take the sentence “This sentence is not true.” If it is neither true nor false, then it is not true, which is just what it says, so it is true after all. This “strengthened Liar” has defeated a long line of solutions.
items.r_zh: 自我指涉本身是無害的：「這個句子有八個字」明明白白是真的。而且這條出路會直接繞回原地。看這個句子：「這個句子不是真的。」如果它既不真也不假，那麼它就不是真的，而這正是它說的，所以它終究是真的。這個「強化版說謊者」已經打敗了一長串的解法。

items.o_en: Paradoxes are games with words. Nobody doubts that runners overtake one another or that heaps exist, so nothing is at stake.
items.o_zh: 悖論是文字遊戲。沒有人懷疑跑者會互相超越，也沒有人懷疑沙堆存在，所以這裡沒有什麼要緊的東西。
items.r_en: Nobody doubts the conclusions are false. What is in doubt is which of our own premises is to blame, and finding out has repeatedly been productive: the theory of limits, modern set theory, and Gödel’s theorems all grew out of taking a paradox seriously. The sorites is also a practical matter. Any law that fixes an age of majority or a speed limit has drawn a sharp line through a vague concept.
items.r_zh: 沒有人懷疑那些結論是假的。有疑問的是：該怪我們自己的哪一個前提？而把這件事弄清楚，一再帶來成果：極限理論、現代集合論、哥德爾定理，都是認真對待某個悖論之後長出來的。堆垛悖論也是很實際的事。任何規定成年年齡或速限的法律，都是在一個模糊的概念上畫了一條清楚的線。

said.claim: Zeno set Achilles to race against a tortoise.
said.claim_zh: 芝諾讓阿基里斯跟一隻烏龜賽跑。
said.en: Our earliest source, Aristotle, mentions no tortoise. He says only that the quickest runner cannot overtake the slowest, and the name “Achilles” tells us who the quick one was. The tortoise appears in later commentators and has been in every retelling since. Zeno’s own words are lost, so we cannot say what example he used.
said.zh: 我們最早的史料亞里斯多德並沒有提到烏龜。他只說跑得最快的追不上最慢的，而「阿基里斯」這個名字告訴我們快的那個是誰。烏龜出現在後來的註釋者筆下，從此每一次轉述都有牠。芝諾自己的話已經失傳，所以我們沒辦法說他用的是什麼例子。

terms.d_en: An apparently sound argument for an unacceptable conclusion.
terms.d_zh: 一個看來健全的論證，卻導出無法接受的結論。

terms.d_en: Refuting a claim by deriving an absurdity from it. Zeno used it against the belief in motion.
terms.d_zh: 從一個主張推出荒謬，藉此反駁它。芝諾用它來反對「運動存在」這個信念。

terms.d_en: The value that the partial sums of a series approach as closely as one likes.
terms.d_zh: 一個級數的部分和可以任意接近的那個值。

terms.d_en: An infinite series whose partial sums have a finite limit.
terms.d_zh: 部分和有有限極限的無窮級數。

terms.d_en: An infinite sequence of tasks completed in a finite time.
terms.d_zh: 在有限時間內完成的無窮多個任務。

terms.d_en: A sentence’s referring to itself, as in the Liar.
terms.d_zh: 句子指涉它自己，例如說謊者悖論。

terms.d_en: A language used to talk about another language, including about which of its sentences are true.
terms.d_zh: 用來談論另一個語言的語言，包括談論後者哪些句子為真。

terms.d_en: A paradox that proceeds by many small, individually harmless steps.
terms.d_zh: 靠許多個別看來無害的小步驟推進的悖論。

terms.d_en: The feature of a word that has borderline cases and no sharp boundary.
terms.d_zh: 一個詞有邊界個案、卻沒有明確界線的特性。

vocab.eg: Since a sound argument cannot have a false conclusion, something must give way.
vocab.eg_zh: 既然健全的論證不可能有假的結論，總得有什麼東西讓步。

vocab.zh: 硬著頭皮接受（不討喜的結論）
vocab.eg: Philosophers call accepting the incredible conclusion biting the bullet.
vocab.eg_zh: 哲學家把接受那個難以置信的結論叫作「咬子彈」。

vocab.eg: The quickest runner can never overtake the slowest.
vocab.eg_zh: 跑得最快的永遠追不上最慢的。

vocab.eg: By the time Achilles has covered the hundred, the other has crept forward ten.
vocab.eg_zh: 等阿基里斯跑完這一百公尺，對方已經往前爬了十公尺。

vocab.eg: Achilles is always on the point of drawing level and never does.
vocab.eg_zh: 阿基里斯永遠就要追平，卻永遠沒有追平。

vocab.eg: Infinitely many distances need not add up to an infinite amount.
vocab.eg_zh: 無窮多段距離，加起來不必是無窮大。

vocab.eg: Many philosophers think this dissolves the paradox.
vocab.eg_zh: 許多哲學家認為這樣就化解了悖論。

vocab.eg: What is at stake is whether space and time are as the mathematics describes them.
vocab.eg_zh: 真正牽涉到的是：空間與時間是不是像數學所描述的那樣。

vocab.eg: The same structure turned up in the foundations of mathematics.
vocab.eg_zh: 同一種結構出現在數學的基礎裡。

vocab.eg: Ordinary English falls short of that standard.
vocab.eg_zh: 日常的英語達不到那個標準。

quiz.q: According to the essay, what are the three possible responses to a paradox?
options: Reject a premise, reject a step, or accept the conclusion.
Ignore it, laugh at it, or change the subject.
Translate it, date it, or attribute it.
Prove it, publish it, or teach it.

quiz.q: Which assumption of Zeno’s does the mathematics of limits refute?
options: That infinitely many intervals must add up to an infinite total.
That Achilles is faster than the tortoise.
That the tortoise has a head start.
That a line can be divided.

quiz.q: What is Thomson’s lamp meant to show?
options: That completing infinitely many tasks may be impossible even when the times have a finite sum.
That electricity was unknown to the Greeks.
That the series one half plus one quarter and so on has no sum.
That lamps cannot be switched quickly.

quiz.q: How did Tarski respond to the Liar?
options: No language can contain its own truth predicate.
The Liar is simply false.
Sentences cannot refer to anything.
Truth does not exist.

quiz.q: Why does the essay call the sorites a practical matter?
options: Laws must draw sharp lines through vague concepts.
Sand is used in building.
Heaps are difficult to count.
Greek merchants sold grain by the heap.

write.en: Which premise of the Achilles would you reject, and why? Answer in about 150 words, and say what your answer commits you to believing about space and time.
write.zh: 阿基里斯論證的哪一個前提你會否定？為什麼？用大約 150 個英文字回答，並說明你的答案讓你對空間與時間必須相信什麼。

write.en: Run a sorites argument on a word that matters to you, such as “adult,” “fluent,” or “rich.” Where would you draw the line, and can you defend drawing it there and not one step earlier?
write.zh: 拿一個對你重要的詞（例如「成年」「流利」「有錢」）跑一次堆垛論證。你會把線畫在哪裡？你能為「畫在這裡、而不是早一步」辯護嗎？

write.en: “This sentence is false.” Explain to a friend, in plain English and without technical terms, why it is a problem.
write.zh: 「這個句子是假的。」用淺白的英文、不用術語，向朋友解釋為什麼這是個問題。

paras.en: Around 200 CE the Indian philosopher Nāgārjuna opened the second chapter of his Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way with an argument that could be mistaken for Zeno’s. What has already been traversed is not being traversed. What has not yet been traversed is not being traversed. And apart from these two there is no third stretch, “being traversed now,” to be found. In Kumārajīva’s Chinese: 已去無有去，未去亦無去，離已去未去，去時亦無去. Two centuries later his Chinese follower Sengzhao drew the conclusion in a famous line: the whirlwind that topples mountains is forever still, and the rivers that race to the sea do not flow.
paras.zh: 大約西元 200 年，印度哲學家龍樹在《中論》第二品開頭提出了一個論證，很容易被誤認成芝諾的。已經走過的路段，不是「正在走」的。還沒走到的路段，也不是「正在走」的。而在這兩者之外，找不到第三段「此刻正在走」的路。鳩摩羅什的漢譯是：「已去無有去，未去亦無去，離已去未去，去時亦無去。」兩個世紀後，他的中國後學僧肇在一句名言裡引出結論：「旋嵐偃嶽而常靜，江河兢注而不流。」

paras.en: The resemblance is real and the purposes are opposite. Zeno argued against motion in order to defend Parmenides’ single unchanging reality. Nāgārjuna has no such reality to defend. His target is the assumption that a mover, a motion, and a path each exist with a nature of their own (svabhāva); grant that assumption, he argues, and motion becomes impossible, so the assumption has to go. People walk, conventionally speaking, and nothing in the argument denies it. Where Zeno accepts the conclusion and gives up change, Nāgārjuna uses the same kind of reductio to give up fixed essences, and that leaves him with a world in which there is nothing except change. Of the three responses to a paradox, he makes the first, and the premise he rejects is one that most of his readers had never noticed they held (Dharma and the West, D8 and D9).
paras.zh: 相似是真的，目的卻相反。芝諾反對運動，是為了捍衛巴門尼德那個唯一而不變的實在。龍樹沒有這樣的實在要捍衛。他瞄準的是一個預設：行走的人、行走這件事、所走的路，各自有它自己的本性（自性，svabhāva）。他論證說，一旦承認這個預設，運動就變得不可能，所以該放棄的是這個預設。就世俗的說法而言，人是會走路的，這個論證絲毫沒有否認這一點。芝諾接受結論而放棄了變化；龍樹用同一種歸謬法放棄的是固定的本質，結果留給他的是一個除了變化別無他物的世界。在回應悖論的三種方式裡，他採取的是第一種；而他否定的那個前提，是大多數讀者從沒察覺自己抱持著的（佛法與西方哲學 D8、D9）。

further.n_zh: 芝諾關於運動的四個論證，兩頁之內全部交代。

philosophers.name: Socrates
philosophers.tag_en: The man who wrote nothing and changed what philosophy is about.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個字也沒寫，卻改變了哲學在問什麼的人。
facts: Sophroniscus, a stoneworker; Phaenarete, a midwife

paras.en: Socrates was born around 470 BCE, when Athens was becoming the richest and most confident city in Greece. His father, Sophroniscus, is said to have worked in stone; his mother, Phaenarete, was a midwife, a fact Plato later turned into a metaphor. He was not rich and not handsome. His friends compared him to a satyr: snub nose, bulging eyes, the same old cloak in every season, and no shoes.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底大約生於西元前 470 年，當時雅典正要成為希臘最富有、最有自信的城邦。據說他的父親索弗羅尼斯科斯是石匠；母親費納瑞特是接生婆，這件事後來被柏拉圖變成一個比喻。他不富有，也不好看。朋友拿他比作森林裡的薩提爾：塌鼻、凸眼，一年四季同一件舊斗篷，而且不穿鞋。

paras.en: He served as a heavy infantryman in three campaigns of the long war with Sparta, at Potidaea, Delium, and Amphipolis. The young aristocrat Alcibiades, whose life he saved at Potidaea, reported that Socrates endured cold and hunger better than anyone and walked off the lost field at Delium so calmly that no enemy cared to approach him.
paras.zh: 在對斯巴達的長年戰爭中，他以重裝步兵的身分參加過三場戰役：波提狄亞、德里昂、安菲波利斯。年輕貴族阿爾基比亞德在波提狄亞被他救過一命；據他說，蘇格拉底比誰都耐寒耐餓，而德里昂兵敗撤退時，他走得那樣從容，敵人沒有一個想靠近。

paras.en: At his trial Socrates explained how his odd career began. His friend Chaerephon had asked the oracle at Delphi whether anyone was wiser than Socrates, and the priestess had answered that no one was. Socrates, aware of having “no wisdom, small or great,” set out to refute the god by finding a wiser man. He questioned politicians, poets, and craftsmen, and found that each believed he knew things he did not. He concluded that the oracle meant something modest: he was wiser only in not mistaking his ignorance for knowledge.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底在法庭上解釋過，他那古怪的生涯是怎麼開始的。他的朋友凱勒豐去德爾菲問神諭：有沒有人比蘇格拉底更有智慧？女祭司回答說沒有。蘇格拉底自知「大小智慧都沒有」，就動身去找一個更有智慧的人，想藉此反駁神。他問過政治家、詩人、工匠，發現每一個都以為自己知道一些其實不知道的事。他的結論是，神諭的意思很平實：他比較有智慧，只在於他沒有把自己的無知誤認為知識。

paras.en: From then on he spent his days in the agora and the gymnasia, questioning anyone who would stop. He charged no fee, which set him apart from the professional teachers called sophists, and he denied that he taught anything at all. He compared himself to a gadfly sent to sting a large and sluggish horse, and to a midwife who helps others deliver ideas while having none of her own.
paras.zh: 從那以後，他整天待在市集與體育場，逢人就問，只要對方肯停下來。他不收學費，這一點使他跟那些稱為「智者」的職業教師不同；他甚至否認自己教過任何東西。他把自己比作一隻牛虻，被派來叮一匹龐大而遲鈍的馬；又比作接生婆，幫別人把想法生出來，自己卻沒有孩子。

paras.en: Athens lost the war in 404 BCE and endured a brutal oligarchy, the Thirty, several of whose leaders had once kept company with Socrates. Socrates himself had defied them: ordered to arrest an innocent man, Leon of Salamis, he simply went home. Democracy was restored the next year, and in 399 three citizens, Meletus, Anytus, and Lycon, brought him to court. The charge, in Plato’s wording, was that he “corrupts the youth” and “does not believe in the gods of the state, but has other new divinities of his own.”
paras.zh: 西元前 404 年雅典戰敗，接著經歷了殘暴的寡頭統治「三十人僭主」，其中幾位領袖從前跟蘇格拉底來往過。蘇格拉底自己倒是違抗過他們：他們命令他去逮捕一個無辜的人，薩拉米斯的勒翁，他直接回家了。第二年民主政體恢復；西元前 399 年，美勒托斯、安尼托斯、呂孔三位公民把他告上法庭。照柏拉圖的記載，罪名是他「敗壞青年」，並且「不信城邦所信的神，另立自己的新神」。

paras.en: A jury of several hundred citizens found him guilty by a narrow margin; had thirty votes gone the other way, he says, he would have been acquitted. Asked to propose his own penalty, he suggested free meals at public expense, then a small fine. The jury chose death. He refused a chance to escape, arguing that a citizen who has accepted the laws all his life may not break them when they turn against him, and a month later he drank the hemlock among his friends. In Plato’s account his last words were a reminder to pay a debt: “Crito, we owe a cock to Asclepius.”
paras.zh: 由數百位公民組成的陪審團以些微差距判他有罪；他說，只要有三十票投向另一邊，他就無罪了。輪到他自己提議刑罰時，他先提議由公家供他免費用餐，後來才改口說可以繳一筆小額罰金。陪審團選了死刑。他拒絕了逃亡的機會，理由是：一個公民一輩子都接受法律，就不能在法律轉而對他不利的時候違反它。一個月後，他在朋友圍繞之下喝了毒芹汁。照柏拉圖的記述，他最後一句話是提醒朋友還一筆債：「克里托，我們還欠阿斯克勒庇俄斯一隻公雞。」

idea.title_en: The central idea: knowing what you do not know
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：知道自己不知道

paras.en: Before Socrates, Greek thinkers had mostly asked what the world is made of. Socrates asked how to live, and he asked it in a new way. He assumed that anyone who is good at something can say what he is doing. A doctor can explain health; a brave man ought to be able to explain courage. When the explanation collapses under questioning, the person’s confidence has been shown to rest on nothing, and the search can start.
paras.zh: 在蘇格拉底之前，希臘思想家問的多半是世界由什麼構成。蘇格拉底問的是人該怎麼活，而且用一種新的方式問。他假定：一個人真的擅長一件事，就說得出自己在做什麼。醫生能解釋健康；勇敢的人應該能解釋勇敢。當這個解釋在追問之下垮掉，就表示這個人的自信沒有根據，而尋找可以開始了。

paras.en: Behind the method lies a bold thesis, usually called Socratic intellectualism: virtue is a kind of knowledge. If you really knew what was good for you, you would do it; so no one does wrong willingly, and all wrongdoing is a form of ignorance. That is why examining beliefs was, for him, a moral task and not an academic one.
paras.zh: 這套方法背後有一個大膽的主張，通常稱為蘇格拉底的「主知主義」：德行是一種知識。如果你真的知道什麼對自己是好的，你就會去做；所以沒有人是自願作惡的，一切過錯都是某種無知。這就是為什麼對他來說，省察信念是道德的工作，不是學院的工作。

quote.en: …the unexamined life is not worth living…
quote.note_en: Spoken after the guilty verdict, to explain why he would not accept exile on condition of silence.
quote.note_zh: 說於有罪判決之後，用來解釋他為什麼不接受「閉嘴就可以流亡」的條件。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: weakness of will

paras.en: If virtue is knowledge, it should be impossible to know what is best and do otherwise. Yet this seems to happen every day: the smoker knows, the procrastinator knows. The Greeks called it akrasia, lack of self-mastery. Aristotle, who admired Socrates, said bluntly that the Socratic view is at odds with what we plainly observe (Nicomachean Ethics VII.2).
paras.zh: 如果德行就是知識，那麼「明知什麼最好卻不去做」應該是不可能的。可是這種事似乎天天發生：抽菸的人知道，拖延的人也知道。希臘人稱之為 akrasia，缺乏自制。亞里斯多德很敬佩蘇格拉底，卻直截了當地說，蘇格拉底的看法跟我們明明看到的事實不合（《尼各馬可倫理學》卷七第二章）。

paras.en: A Socratic can reply that the smoker does not fully know: at the moment of choice the nearer pleasure looks larger than it is, the way a nearby object looks bigger than a distant one, and what he lacks is an art of measuring (Protagoras 356c–357b). Whether that reply rescues the thesis or merely redefines “knowledge” is still disputed.
paras.zh: 蘇格拉底這一邊可以回答：抽菸的人並不是「完全知道」。在選擇的當下，近處的快樂看起來比實際大，就像近的東西看起來比遠的大；他缺的是一門「衡量的技藝」（《普羅塔哥拉篇》356c–357b）。這個回答究竟救回了原來的主張，還是只是把「知識」重新定義了一次，至今仍有爭論。

paras.en: Because Socrates wrote nothing, everything we know comes through others, and they do not agree. Aristophanes, writing while Socrates was alive, shows a ridiculous charlatan in a basket. Xenophon shows a sensible moral adviser. Plato shows a philosophical genius, and he keeps using “Socrates” as a character for decades, long after the views expressed have become Plato’s own. Scholars usually treat the early, short dialogues that end in aporia (Apology, Euthyphro, Laches) as closest to the historical man, and admit that this is a judgment and not a certainty.
paras.zh: 因為蘇格拉底什麼都沒寫，我們知道的一切都是經由別人，而這些人的說法並不一致。阿里斯托芬在蘇格拉底還活著的時候寫劇本，劇中的他是個吊在籃子裡的可笑騙子。色諾芬筆下的他，是個通情達理的道德顧問。柏拉圖筆下的他是哲學天才；而且柏拉圖把「蘇格拉底」這個角色用了幾十年，用到後來，角色口中的見解早已是柏拉圖自己的。學者通常把早期那些以困惑收場的短篇對話錄（《申辯篇》《歐緒弗洛篇》《拉凱斯篇》）視為最接近歷史上的那個人，同時也承認這是一種判斷，不是定論。

said.claim: “The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing.”
said.claim_zh: 「唯一真正的智慧，是知道自己一無所知。」
said.en: No ancient source has Socrates say this. It paraphrases Apology 21d and 23a–b, where he interprets the oracle to mean that human wisdom is worth little, and that the wisest person is the one who, like Socrates, recognizes this.
said.zh: 沒有任何古代文獻記載蘇格拉底說過這句話。它是《申辯篇》21d 與 23a–b 的改寫；在那裡，他把神諭解釋為：人的智慧沒什麼價值，而最有智慧的，是像蘇格拉底這樣看出這一點的人。

paras.en: The two were near contemporaries and never heard of each other. Both wrote nothing, taught by conversation, took no fee, and were remembered through dialogues composed by followers. Both held that the root of going wrong is a kind of ignorance: for Socrates, not knowing what is good; for the Buddha, avijjā, not seeing things as they are.
paras.zh: 這兩個人的年代相去不遠，彼此從未聽過對方。兩人都沒有著作，都用談話教人，都不收費，也都靠弟子編寫的對話被後人記得。兩人都認為，人走錯路的根源是某種無知：在蘇格拉底是不知道什麼是善；在佛陀是無明（avijjā），沒有如實看見事物。

paras.en: The difference shows in the remedy. For Socrates the cure is argument, and he seems to think that seeing the truth is enough to act on it. The Buddhist path adds training of attention and conduct, on the view that craving does not dissolve merely because one has reached a correct conclusion. That is, in effect, a Buddhist answer to the problem of akrasia.
paras.zh: 差別在藥方。蘇格拉底的藥是論證，而且他似乎認為，看見了真理就足以照著去做。佛教的道路多了對注意力與行為的訓練（戒與定），因為它認為，貪愛不會只因為人得出了正確的結論就消散。這其實就是佛教對「意志薄弱」問題的回答。

terms.d_en: A paid traveling teacher of rhetoric and public skill in fifth-century Greece.
terms.d_zh: 西元前五世紀希臘收費授課、教授修辭與公共事務能力的巡迴教師。

terms.d_en: His habit of professing ignorance and praising the other speaker’s expertise before testing it.
terms.d_zh: 他在檢驗對方之前，先自稱無知、稱讚對方內行的習慣。

terms.d_en: Describing teaching that draws ideas out of the learner by questions (Theaetetus 149a–151d).
terms.d_zh: 形容用提問把想法從學習者身上引出來的教法（《泰阿泰德篇》149a–151d）。

terms.d_en: Acting against one’s own better judgment.
terms.d_zh: 違背自己較好的判斷去行動。

terms.d_en: The inner sign Socrates said warned him against certain actions; it only ever said no.
terms.d_zh: 蘇格拉底說會警告他別做某些事的內在徵兆；它只會說「不」。

terms.d_en: The difficulty of recovering the historical Socrates from conflicting sources.
terms.d_zh: 從彼此衝突的史料中還原歷史上的蘇格拉底，這件事的困難。

quiz.q: How did Socrates interpret the oracle’s statement that no one was wiser than he?
options: He alone did not mistake his ignorance for knowledge.
He possessed secret knowledge from the gods.

quiz.q: What does “Socratic intellectualism” claim?
options: Virtue is a kind of knowledge, so no one does wrong willingly.
Only intellectuals can be virtuous.
Knowledge is impossible.

quiz.q: Why is it hard to know what the historical Socrates thought?
options: He wrote nothing, and the surviving portraits disagree.
His books were burned after the trial.
Plato never mentions him.

philosophers.name: Aristotle
philosophers.tag_en: He divided knowledge into the subjects we still study, and invented the science that checks reasoning in all of them.
philosophers.tag_zh: 他把知識分成我們至今還在讀的科目，並且發明了檢查一切科目推理的那門學問。
facts: 322 BCE, Chalcis, on the island of Euboea
Nicomachus, physician to the king of Macedon

paras.en: Aristotle was born in 384 BCE at Stagira, a small town in the north of Greece. His father, Nicomachus, was physician to the king of Macedon, and it is tempting to see the doctor’s son in the philosopher who later dissected cuttlefish and classified some five hundred kinds of animal. Orphaned young, he was sent at seventeen to Athens to study at Plato’s Academy, and he stayed for about twenty years, until Plato died.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德西元前 384 年生於希臘北部的小鎮斯塔基拉。父親尼各馬可是馬其頓國王的御醫；這位哲學家日後解剖烏賊、替大約五百種動物分類，讓人很難不在他身上看到醫生兒子的影子。他年少失怙，十七歲被送到雅典，進柏拉圖的學院求學，一待大約二十年，直到柏拉圖去世。

paras.en: He was never a citizen of Athens and could not own property there. He was also never simply a disciple. Where Plato looked past the changing world to eternal Forms, Aristotle came to hold that the form of a thing is found in the thing, and that knowledge begins from careful observation of particulars. A later saying sums up his attitude: Plato is dear to me, but truth is dearer. The wording is medieval; the thought is his (Nicomachean Ethics I.6).
paras.zh: 他始終不是雅典公民，在那裡不能擁有產業。他也從來不只是個門徒。柏拉圖把目光越過變動的世界，望向永恆的「理型」；亞里斯多德後來則主張，事物的形式就在事物之中，知識要從仔細觀察個別事物開始。後世有句話概括了他的態度：「吾愛吾師，吾更愛真理。」這個措辭是中世紀的，意思卻是他自己的（《尼各馬可倫理學》卷一第六章）。

paras.en: When Plato died in 347, Aristotle left Athens. He spent several years on the coast of Asia Minor and on the island of Lesbos, where, with his friend Theophrastus, he did much of the biological research that fills a quarter of his surviving work. Around 343 Philip of Macedon invited him to tutor his thirteen-year-old son, the future Alexander the Great. What the philosopher taught the conqueror, and how much of it stayed, nobody knows.
paras.zh: 西元前 347 年柏拉圖去世，亞里斯多德離開雅典。他在小亞細亞沿岸與列斯伏斯島住了幾年；他現存著作有四分之一是生物學，其中大部分的研究，就是在那裡跟朋友泰奧弗拉斯托斯一起做的。大約西元前 343 年，馬其頓的腓力請他去教自己十三歲的兒子，也就是日後的亞歷山大大帝。哲學家教了征服者什麼、留下了多少，沒有人知道。

paras.en: In 335 he returned to Athens and opened his own school in a public gymnasium called the Lyceum. Its members were nicknamed Peripatetics, probably from the covered walk, the peripatos, where they talked. The Lyceum was something new: a research institute, with a library, collections of specimens, and teams compiling the constitutions of 158 Greek cities.
paras.zh: 西元前 335 年他回到雅典，在一座名叫呂克昂的公共體育場開了自己的學校。學校的成員被稱為「逍遙學派」，這個綽號大概來自他們邊走邊談的那條有頂走廊（peripatos）。呂克昂是一種新的東西：一所研究機構，有圖書館、有標本收藏，還有團隊在彙編 158 個希臘城邦的政制。

paras.en: What survives from those years is about thirty treatises, roughly a third of what he wrote. They are not polished books. They read like lecture notes, dense and abrupt, and the dialogues he published for the public, which Cicero praised as a golden river of eloquence, are lost. When Alexander died in 323, Athens turned on everything Macedonian, and a charge of impiety was prepared against Aristotle. He withdrew to Chalcis, reportedly saying that he would not let the Athenians sin twice against philosophy, and died there the following year.
paras.zh: 那些年留下來的是大約三十部專論，約佔他全部著作的三分之一。它們不是精心修飾的書，讀起來像講課筆記，濃縮而突兀；他為一般讀者發表的對話錄，西塞羅曾讚美為「雄辯的金色河流」，卻全都失傳了。西元前 323 年亞歷山大去世，雅典轉而敵視一切跟馬其頓有關的東西，有人準備以「不敬神」的罪名控告亞里斯多德。他退居卡爾基斯，據說留下一句話：他不讓雅典人對哲學犯第二次罪。第二年他在那裡去世。

timeline: 亞歷山大去世；被控不敬神

idea.title_en: The central idea: Reasoning has a form
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：推理有它的形式

paras.en: Aristotle’s logical works were later bundled under the title Organon, “the tool,” and the name is exact. He did not regard logic as one science among others. It was the instrument every science uses. His discovery was that whether a conclusion follows depends on the arrangement of terms in an argument and not on what the terms mean, so that arrangements can be studied systematically. In the Prior Analytics he worked through every combination of two premises of four kinds, identified those that yield a conclusion of necessity, and showed how the rest reduce to a few basic patterns. No one had attempted anything like it. Near the end of the Organon he says so himself: on this subject there was nothing at all before him to build on.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德的邏輯著作後來被合編在《工具論》（Organon）這個標題下，這個名字很精確。他不把邏輯看成眾多科學當中的一門；它是每一門科學都要用的工具。他的發現是：結論推不推得出來，取決於論證裡詞項的排列，而不是詞項的意思，所以排列方式可以有系統地研究。在《前分析篇》裡，他把四種命題兩兩組合成前提的每一種情形都走過一遍，辨認出哪些必然得出結論，並證明其餘的可以化約為少數幾個基本樣式。在他之前沒有人做過類似的事。《工具論》接近結尾處，他自己也這麼說：在這個題目上，他之前完全沒有可以憑藉的東西。

paras.en: The same habit of mind runs through everything else he touched. To understand a thing is to grasp its causes, and he distinguished four: what it is made of, what form it has, what brought it about, and what it is for. To live well is to exercise, over a whole life, the excellences proper to a human being, which is what he meant by eudaimonia. To be good at feeling and acting is to hit the mean between too much and too little, as courage lies between cowardice and rashness. In each field he begins by collecting the opinions of “the many and the wise,” sorts out the puzzles, and builds from there.
paras.zh: 同一種思考習慣貫穿他碰過的一切。了解一樣東西，就是掌握它的原因；他分出四種：它由什麼構成、有什麼形式、由什麼促成、為了什麼目的。活得好，就是在一整個人生中發揮人之為人所特有的卓越，這是他說的 eudaimonia（幸福、人的興盛）。在感受與行動上做得好，就是命中太多與太少之間的「中道」，就像勇敢位於懦弱與魯莽之間。在每個領域，他都先蒐集「多數人與有智慧的人」的意見，理清其中的疑難，再從那裡往上蓋。

quote.en: All men by nature desire to know.
quote.ref: Aristotle, Metaphysics I.1, 980a, tr. W. D. Ross
quote.note_en: The first sentence of the Metaphysics. His evidence is that we enjoy seeing things even when it is of no use to us.
quote.note_zh: 《形上學》的第一句。他的證據是：即使沒有用處，我們也喜歡看東西。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: The logic was too small
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：這套邏輯太小了

paras.en: For two thousand years Aristotle’s logic was treated as finished. Kant wrote in 1787 that since Aristotle logic had not needed to retrace a single step, and had not been able to advance one either. Less than a century later it was shown to be a fragment. The syllogism handles statements built from two terms, “all A are B.” It cannot handle relations. From “a horse is an animal” it follows that the head of a horse is the head of an animal, and, as Augustus De Morgan pointed out, no syllogism can prove it. Nor can it deal with statements that mix “every” and “some,” such as “everyone loves someone,” on which mathematics depends. In 1879 Gottlob Frege published a logic that could do all this, and Aristotle’s system became one small corner of it.
paras.zh: 有兩千年之久，亞里斯多德的邏輯被當成已經完成的學問。康德在 1787 年寫道，自亞里斯多德以來，邏輯沒有必要後退一步，也沒能前進一步。不到一百年後，它被證明只是一個片段。三段論處理由兩個詞項構成的陳述：「所有 A 都是 B」。它處理不了「關係」。從「馬是動物」可以推出「馬的頭是動物的頭」，而正如德摩根指出的，沒有任何三段論證得出這一點。它也對付不了混用「每一個」與「某一個」的陳述，例如「每個人都愛著某個人」，而數學正需要這種陳述。1879 年，弗雷格發表了一套能做到這一切的邏輯，亞里斯多德的系統成了其中的一個小角落。

paras.en: A second objection concerns his authority and not his logic. Because he was right about so much, his mistakes were protected for centuries: that heavier bodies fall faster, that the earth sits still at the center, that some people are slaves by nature and that women are naturally subordinate. The fault lies partly with his followers, since Aristotle himself held that argument must give way to observation. But the last two claims are his own, argued for in the Politics, and they show how a careful reasoner can mistake the arrangements of his own society for facts of nature.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁針對的是他的權威，不是他的邏輯。因為他對的地方太多，他的錯誤被保護了好幾個世紀：重的物體落得比較快；地球靜止在中心；有些人天生就是奴隸，而女人天生居於從屬。過錯有一部分在他的追隨者，因為亞里斯多德自己主張，論證必須向觀察讓步。但最後兩項是他本人的主張，在《政治學》裡有論證；它們顯示，一個細心的推理者可以怎樣把自己社會的安排，誤認為自然的事實。

problem.title_zh: 這些書是怎麼傳到我們手上的

paras.en: The treatises we read were probably never meant for publication. According to an ancient story, Aristotle’s manuscripts passed to Theophrastus and then to heirs who hid them in a cellar, where they lay for some two centuries before being brought to Rome and edited by Andronicus of Rhodes in the first century BCE. Whatever the truth of the story, the arrangement and many of the titles we use are the editor’s. “Metaphysics” itself is his label for the books placed after the Physics. In the Latin West most of Aristotle was then lost for centuries and returned in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, largely through Arabic scholarship, with the commentaries of Ibn Sīnā and Ibn Rushd. To medieval readers he was simply “the Philosopher.”
paras.zh: 我們讀到的這些專論，大概從來不是為了出版而寫的。照一個古代的說法，亞里斯多德的手稿傳給泰奧弗拉斯托斯，再傳給後人，後人把它們藏在地窖裡，一放大約兩個世紀，才被帶到羅馬，在西元前一世紀由羅得島的安德羅尼科編訂。不管這個故事有幾分真，我們現在用的編排與許多書名都出自這位編者；「形上學」這個名字，就是他給排在《物理學》之後那幾卷書的標籤。此後在拉丁語的西方，亞里斯多德的大部分著作失傳了好幾個世紀，到十二、十三世紀才回來，而且主要是經由阿拉伯學術，連同伊本・西那與伊本・魯世德的註釋一起。對中世紀的讀者來說，他就叫「那位哲學家」。

said.claim: “We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.”
said.claim_zh: 「我們反覆做什麼，我們就是什麼。所以卓越不是一個行為，而是一種習慣。」
said.en: These are Will Durant’s words, from his summary of Aristotle’s ethics in The Story of Philosophy (1926). They paraphrase Nicomachean Ethics II.1–4, where Aristotle says that we become just by doing just acts and brave by doing brave acts. The summary is fair. The sentence is not Aristotle’s.
said.zh: 這是威爾・杜蘭的話，出自他在《哲學的故事》（1926）裡對亞里斯多德倫理學的摘要。它轉述的是《尼各馬可倫理學》卷二第一至四章；亞里斯多德在那裡說，我們因為做正義的事而成為正義的人，因為做勇敢的事而成為勇敢的人。這個摘要很公允，但句子不是亞里斯多德寫的。

paras.en: Two comparisons are often made, and both need care. The first is between Aristotle’s mean and the Buddha’s Middle Way. They share a shape and differ in substance. Aristotle’s mean is a point on a scale of feeling or action, different for each person and situation: the right amount of anger, the right amount of giving. The Middle Way (majjhimā paṭipadā) of the first sermon is a path between two ways of life, indulgence in sense pleasure and self-mortification, and it is spelled out as the eightfold path. Aristotle aims at the flourishing of a self. The Buddha’s path leads to seeing that there is no such self to flourish.
paras.zh: 常有人做兩個比較，兩個都需要小心。第一個是亞里斯多德的「中道」與佛陀的「中道」。兩者形狀相同，內容不同。亞里斯多德的中道是感受或行動量尺上的一個點，隨人、隨情境而不同：恰當分量的憤怒，恰當分量的施予。佛陀初轉法輪所說的中道（majjhimā paṭipadā），是兩種生活方式之間的一條路——耽於欲樂與自我折磨——並且具體展開為八正道。亞里斯多德瞄準的是一個自我的興盛；佛陀的道路通向的是看清：並沒有這樣一個可供興盛的自我。

paras.en: The second comparison is closer. Aristotle held that character is formed by repeated action: we become what we practice. Buddhist accounts of karma and of cultivation (bhāvanā) say much the same, and both traditions conclude that ethics is a matter of training and not only of knowing. That is the point on which both part company with Socrates. Which Western ethical theory Buddhist ethics most resembles, Aristotle’s or the utilitarians’, is a live debate among scholars (Dharma and the West, D18).
paras.zh: 第二個比較貼近得多。亞里斯多德主張，品格是由反覆的行動形成的：我們練習什麼，就成為什麼。佛教對業與修習（bhāvanā）的說明，講的幾乎是同一件事；兩個傳統都得出結論：倫理是訓練的事，不只是知道的事。在這一點上，兩者都跟蘇格拉底分道揚鑣。至於佛教倫理最像西方哪一種倫理學理論——亞里斯多德的，還是效益主義的——是學界正在進行的爭論（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

terms.d_en: The traditional name for Aristotle’s six logical treatises.
terms.d_zh: 亞里斯多德六部邏輯專論的傳統總稱。

terms.d_en: Belonging to Aristotle’s school.
terms.d_zh: 屬於亞里斯多德學派的。

terms.d_en: Living and doing well over a whole life; often translated “happiness,” more exactly “flourishing.”
terms.d_zh: 在一整個人生中活得好、做得好；常譯「幸福」，更精確的說法是「興盛」。

terms.d_en: That for the sake of which a thing exists or is done; the root of “teleology.”
terms.d_zh: 事物存在或行為發生所為的目的；teleology（目的論）的字根。

terms.d_en: Material, formal, efficient, and final: four kinds of answer to the question why.
terms.d_zh: 質料因、形式因、動力因、目的因：對「為什麼」的四種回答。

terms.d_en: The right amount, between excess and deficiency, in feeling and action.
terms.d_zh: 感受與行動上，介於過與不及之間的恰當分量。

quiz.q: What was new about the Lyceum?
options: It worked as a research institute, with a library and collections.
It charged the highest fees in Athens.
It taught only mathematics.
It was open only to Athenian citizens.

quiz.q: What did Aristotle discover about arguments?
options: Whether a conclusion follows depends on the arrangement of terms, not on their meaning.
Only arguments about nature can be valid.
Every argument is circular.
Observation is unnecessary.

quiz.q: Why was Aristotle’s logic shown to be incomplete in the nineteenth century?
options: It could not handle relations or statements mixing “every” and “some.”
It contained a contradiction.
It had been mistranslated from Greek.
It relied on experiments.
